headline: EU framework needed to unlock semi-private truck charging | IRU | World Road Transport Organisation
summary_text: · Environment ## IRU and Transport & Environment (T&E) are calling on the European Commission to establish a supportive EU framework for semi-private charging as part of the upcoming review of the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR). In a joint letter to Executive Vice-President Teresa Ribera and Commissioner for Sustainable Transport and Tourism Apostolos Tzitzikostas, IRU and T&E stress the need for a complete charging ecosystem combining public, private depot and semi-private infrastructure. The aim is to unlock additional charging capacity for zero-emission trucks, particularly benefiting small and medium-sized transport operators. While public charging remains essential for journeys beyond operators’ home bases, depot charging will cover a substantial share of their energy needs. Semi-private charging can bridge the gap between fully private and publicly accessible infrastructure by creating incentives for companies to voluntarily open part of their charging capacity at depots, warehouses and logistics hubs to other transport operators. IRU EU Advocacy Director Raluca Marian said, “A successful transition to zero-emission trucks requires a complete charging ecosystem. Semi-private charging offers an opportunity to maximise the use of existing and future infrastructure, while expanding access for smaller operators without their own charging facilities and for companies needing to charge where they conduct business.” ... The organisations call for semi-private charging to be recognised as a distinct category under AFIR, supported by a coherent EU enabling framework to be implemented by Member States. Such a framework should facilitate permitting and grid connections, integrate depot and semi-private charging into national infrastructure and energy planning, and enable access to appropriate EU and national funding and State aid support. Crucially, participation must remain voluntary, with simple and proportionate conditions that allow infrastructure owners to retain control over access and prioritise their own operations, without automatically being treated as public charging operators or electricity suppliers.

Ambak added that the association is open to more members joining its ranks and highlighted its international reach. “The topic of IRFA is to represent the RFS industry and other stakeholders. It could be recommending best practice on security, sustainability, safety, documentation, process and systems, participating in the elaboration of relevant regulations, acting as a contact organisation for authorities, and providing training and information dissemination to the sector.” Issues that the association will aim to address include a recommended standard contract and service level agreement; standards for slot allocation at airport cargo terminals; data standards for cargo on the road to support real-time cargo visibility; sustainability; and improving driver access to facilities at airport cargo terminals. The IRFA said that slot allocation at airports is one of the biggest challenges faced by RFS operators, which “lose many truck and driver hours due to insufficient slot allocation at airport cargo terminals…which often further can lead to service failures as flight connections are missed or ready for pick-up promises not met”. “[The] IRFA wishes, with the ground handlers, to create solid standards for slot allocation for truck loading and off-loading, reducing service failures and increasing service efficiency,” the association said. A standardised contract, meanwhile, would help tender, contracting and service follow-up processes for airlines and RFS providers. The contract would act as a framework with commercial terms being negotiated bilaterally between each airline and each RFS provider. On sustainability, the association said it aimed to help with the development of more charging points and hydrogen refuelling stations at airports, the lack of which is a blockage to the development of more environmentally friendly road operations. Improving driver facilities would help attract more people to the industry, which is currently facing a driver shortage, the members explained. The not-for-profit organisation is in the process of being registered in Luxembourg.

headline: Daimler Truck maps what it takes to scale electric trucks - FreightWaves
summary_text: HANNOVER, Germany — Daimler Truck laid out what it says Europe needs to move battery-electric and hydrogen trucks from early adopters into mainstream fleets. It includes public megawatt chargers, hydrogen stations built for trucks and road tolls that reward zero-emission vehicles. CEO Karin Rådström made the case at the company’s Media Night in Hanover, Germany, ahead of IAA Transportation 2026. Mercedes-Benz Trucks held about 38% of Europe’s market for locally CO2-free medium- and heavy-duty trucks in the first half of 2026, and customers have driven the eActros 600 more than 160 million kilometers since series production began at the end of 2024, the company said. “Today, there are over 60 electric or zero-emission trucks available in the market, and over 25 different zero-emission bus models from us and from our competitors,” Rådström said. “So our industry has clearly delivered.” Heavy-duty battery-electric trucks took 2% of Europe’s market in 2025, according to Daimler Truck, which estimates about 35% of new trucks would need to run on batteries or hydrogen by 2030 to meet EU CO2 targets. The European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association’s full-year 2025 commercial vehicle registration data, released Jan. 29, put all electrically chargeable trucks above 3.5 tonnes at 4.2% of the EU market, up from 2.3% a year earlier. Customers hold back for two reasons, Rådström said: infrastructure and cost parity with diesel. ... ## Chargers, hydrogen stations and tolls Europe has fewer than 2,000 public truck charge points today, most of them standard CCS chargers, Rådström said. By 2030, she said, it needs 35,000 megawatt charging points to support the battery-electric trucks the CO2 targets require. Europe has around 187 hydrogen stations, most supplying only 350 bar, which Rådström said is not suitable for trucks. She said Europe needs 1,000 by 2030. On cost, Rådström pointed to CO2-based road tolls. In Germany, the toll difference between a diesel truck and an electric truck comes out to about 33 to 35 cents per kilometer, which she said helps offset the higher investment cost. Only 13 of the EU’s 27 member states have adopted CO2-based tolls, she said, and fewer than a handful of those set a meaningful gap between electric and diesel. ... Stefan Hohm, chief development officer at Dachser, the German logistics provider, said on stage that the company has 25 emission-free delivery areas in Europe and more than 200 battery-electric trucks on the road, including more than 160 Mercedes-Benz Actros models. “We are proud to have more than 200 battery-electric trucks on the road, but the truth is we run more than 15,000,” Hohm said. “So this is only a beginning. And financing the first generation of battery-electric vehicles remains the main hurdle for our transport partners.” Hohm called grid access and capacity the main pain point. A Dachser network study found almost all of its 300 European branches have access to 1 to 3 megawatts of grid capacity, he said, and in Germany the company deals with 800 energy providers. He wants clear timelines and binding commitments from them. Toll gaps between diesel and electric trucks vary by country: almost 33 cents per kilometer in Germany, nothing in France and almost €1 in Switzerland, Hohm said. He wants a stable framework that holds for at least five to six years. ... The eActros Lowliner, a battery-electric tractor with a low fifth-wheel height for high-volume mega trailers, opened for orders Sept. 15, with series production at the Mercedes-Benz plant in Wörth, Germany, set for the second quarter of 2027. The three-battery version offers around 500 kilometers of range at full load, and megawatt charging arriving in the second half of 2027 will take it from 10% to 80% in under 30 minutes, the company said. On hydrogen, a small series of 100 Mercedes-Benz NextGenH2 fuel-cell trucks enters customer operations from the end of 2026, with Dachser as the first customer. Hohm said the first truck will run two shifts out of Malsch, near Karlsruhe, with a target of 220,000 kilometers a year. ... ## The regulatory review Daimler Truck is asking the EU for an early review of its heavy-duty CO2 regulation, with the 2030 target tied to infrastructure rollout and customers’ total cost of ownership. That target calls for a 43% cut in CO2 emissions from new heavy-duty vehicles compared with 2019, and the Council of the EU adopted a temporary flexibility on March 30 that lets manufacturers accumulate credits from 2025 through 2029 by beating their own annual targets. The same release said the core rules are due for revision in 2027. The company puts the cost of falling short at about €120 million in penalties for each percentage point Mercedes-Benz Trucks misses. Rådström said a 10-point miss “effectively would wipe out the full profitability globally of Mercedes-Benz Trucks for that year.”

headline: Uber Freight bets on European 4PL services, as distinction with 3PL blurs - The Loadstar
summary_text: Uber Freight is stepping up investment in its European 4PL business, despite acknowledging that shippers increasingly care less about whether their logistics provider is labelled a 3PL or 4PL. The company yesterday announced plans to expand its European fourth-party logistics operation, investing in technology, operations, and staff, and adding a second location, with a new control tower and operations hub in Krakow to open next year. It has also appointed Mike Doucleff as head of Europe, affective 28 September. Uber Freight said the number of new 4PL deals it won in Europe doubled last year, and it sees further opportunities among North American customers looking to reduce the number of logistics partners they use globally. The investment comes as Uber Freight’s wider business has returned to top-line growth, although it remains loss-making. Freight revenue jumped 25% year on year, to $1.58bn, in the second quarter, while the division reported a $24m operating loss. But it remains committed to the European expansion. Uber Freight is investing further resources to managed transportation and 4PL, while its overall freight division is still working towards sustainable profitability. Its first 4PL engagement, designed to span North America and Europe, is with chemicals manufacturer OXEA, covering transportation in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Europe. Uber Freight’s European 4PL operation was inherited through its acquisition of Transplace, and is separate from the European freight brokerage business it sold in 2020. However, the expansion comes amid an increasingly blurred distinction between the traditional roles of 3PLs and 4PLs – something the company itself acknowledges. “We’re seeing the lines blur,” a spokesperson told The Loadstar. “Customers don’t necessarily think about their problems as ‘3PL’ or ‘4PL’ – they’re looking for partners that can solve more of their transportation needs and help them manage increasingly complex networks.” Indeed, 30% of Uber Freight customers now use two or more of its services, up from 24% last year, while more than 80% of its large managed transportation customers have also used its capacity solutions. “The label matters less to the customer than the outcome,” the spokesperson added.

headline: European contract and spot rates accelerate as fuel costs are passed on | IRU | World Road Transport Organisation
summary_text: ## The IRU x Upply x Ti Q2 2026 report shows that European contract and spot markets have accelerated sharply, breaking with the softer conditions seen through late 2025 and in Q1 2026. Contract rates rose to 148 index points, up 7.9 points quarter on quarter (QoQ) and 15.2 points year on year (YoY). Spot rates climbed even more steeply, reaching 146.8 index points, up 14.6 points QoQ and 13.9 points YoY, nearly double contract rate's quarterly pace. After three quarters of divergence, both markets are now moving up together, driven primarily by cost rather than demand. - EU diesel prices averaged EUR 1.94 per litre in Q2, up 12% QoQ and 27% YoY, peaking at EUR 2.19 in April before falling back to EUR 1.76 in the last week of June, 17% below the end of Q1 - Operating costs rose by almost 10% YoY and 4.9% QoQ, according to the French government’s Comité National Routier’s (CNR) long-haul truck index, with the index spiking from 166.29 in February to 182.03 in April - Road trade volumes between major EU economies fell 1.6% YoY in Q2, a far shallower decline than the 8% recorded in Q1, pointing to volumes stabilising rather than deteriorating - Driver availability remains a structural capacity constraint: 13% of truck driver positions are unfilled in Europe, equivalent to around 502,000 positions, according to IRU's 2025 driver shortage report - Continued upward pressure through H2 2026 is expected, as high operating costs are passed through, though softening industrial demand should cap how far rates can rise - The Road Freight Sentiment Index for Q2 stood at 28.3, up by 11.4 points from Q1 and its highest level on record, indicating strengthened expectations that European road freight rates will rise over the next three months ... Road trade volumes between major EU economies fell 1.6% YoY in Q2, with the steepest declines on two of the largest corridors: Germany-France (-3.9%) and Spain-France (-3.6%), partly offset by Germany-Poland (+1.5%). That is a far shallower decline than the 8% recorded in Q1. As Q2 is typically among the stronger quarters in tonnage terms, the easing YoY decline points to road volumes levelling off. Measured in tonne-kilometres, the fall may be smaller still, as longer average hauls partially offset lower tonnage. ... Only a handful of markets were shielding carriers from fuel costs. Spain and France operate national fuel indices allowing hauliers to pass diesel costs through to rates, and Italy does so to a more limited extent, but even these mechanisms struggled to keep pace with the speed of the increase. Spanish hauliers, in particular, struggled to recover the increase despite their legal entitlement to do so, prompting the Spanish government to introduce Real Decreto-ley 9/2026, in force since 16 April, which substantially strengthens the mandatory pass-through of fuel cost increases and introduces penalties for non-compliance. EU countries began unwinding relief measures as prices fell. Germany cut fuel duty by around EUR 0.17 per litre for May and June under a EUR 1.6 billion package, while Ireland deployed a EUR 505 million support scheme. Slovakia withdrew its foreign-plate diesel surcharge and purchase limits on 8 May under Commission infringement pressure, and Hungary released 575 million litres of strategic reserves in May before voting to phase out its price cap. Germany's duty cut, Spain's VAT reduction and Poland's fuel VAT cut expired on 30 June.

summary_text: ## Highlights In 2025, total road freight transport in the EU amounted to 1 886 billion tonne-kilometres and nearly 13.3 billion tonnes. In 2025, it increased further, by 0.9% to 1 886 billion tkm (see Table 1 and Figure 1). International transport accounted for almost one quarter (24.4%) of total road freight transport in the EU in 2025. It decreased by 1.5% from 2023 to 2024, followed by a slight increase of 0.3% from 2024 to 2025 (see Table 1). National transport, which represented almost two thirds (62.2%) of the total in 2025, increased by 0.8% in 2024 and 2.2% in 2025. Cross-trade and cabotage transport (together representing 13.4% of the EU total in 2025), fell by 3.7% and 3.0%, respectively, compared with 2024. In 2025, Poland (20.2% of EU total tkm) reconfirmed its position as one of the most important countries for road transport in Europe, ahead of Germany (14.7%) and Spain (14.5%). Together, international transport, cross-trade and cabotage made up 60.0% of Poland's transport performance, while national transport represented 40.0%. ... ## The main goods categories transported in 2025 were the same as in 2024, both in terms of tonnes and tonne-kilometres In terms of tonnage, European road freight transport increased by 1.8% in 2025, compared with 2024 (from 13 057 million tonnes to 13 291 million tonnes – see Table 2). Other important product groups were 'food, beverages and tobacco' (1 611 million tonnes), 'other non-metallic mineral products' (1 602 million tonnes), and 'agricultural, forestry and fishery products' (1 289 million tonnes). The most notable increases between 2024 and 2025 were recorded for ‘coal and lignite; crude petroleum and natural gas’ (up by 17.8%), ‘unidentifiable goods’ (up by 15.7%) and ‘equipment and material utilized in the transport of goods’ (up by 8.6%). At the other end of the scale, significant decreases were recorded for the product groups ‘textiles and textile products; leather and leather products’ (-6.6%), ‘furniture’ (-2.8%) and ‘removals; motor vehicles moved for repair’ (-2.3%). headline: “十五五”时期BOPET薄膜行业市场调研及发展趋势预测报告|新能源|市场规模|产业|规划|指标_新浪财经_新浪新闻
summary_text: 1、BOPET薄膜行业概况 BOPET薄膜（双向拉伸聚酯薄膜）以优质聚酯切片（PET）为主要原料，经干燥、熔融、挤出、铸片后，于特定温度条件下沿纵向与横向同步进行双向拉伸，并经热定型工艺制成具有平衡取向结构的薄膜。该工艺促使分子链有序取向排列，使薄膜兼具高透明度、高拉伸强度、优异的尺寸稳定性及良好的阻氧阻湿性能，被广泛应用于包装、电子电气、光学显示及新能源等领域。我国是全球最大BOPET薄膜生产国，国内产能占全球总产能60%以上，但行业存在低端产能过剩、高端供给不足的结构性矛盾，通用包装膜赛道内卷严重，新能源、光学、电子电气等高附加值功能膜成为行业增长新引擎。 ... OP ... BOPET薄膜产业链上游为石油化工及原材料供应环节，负责提供精对苯二甲酸（PTA）、乙二醇（MEG）等核心基础原料及功能性添加剂；中游为薄膜生产制造环节，通过熔融、双向拉伸、热定型及涂布等核心工艺，将聚酯树脂加工为具备特定物理与化学性能的薄膜产品；下游为终端应用与消费环节，将各类薄膜广泛应用于包装印刷、电子电气、新能源及光学显示等领域。 ... 3、BOPET薄膜行业市场规模分析 2021‑2025年我国BOPET薄膜行业市场规模由382.49亿元小幅增长至383.85亿元，整体基本持平，年复合增长率仅0.09%，期间行业呈现先回落、后修复的走势，2022‑2023年受下游需求走弱、原料价格震荡以及低端产能集中释放影响市场规模阶段性下行，2024‑2025年依靠新能源、光学显示领域高端功能膜需求带动实现回暖；展望2026‑2030年，行业市场规模预计将从410.17亿元扩张至534.85亿元，复合年均增长率达6.86%，行业增长重心持续向新能源、光学显示、电子电气等高附加值赛道倾斜，光伏背板膜、MLCC离型膜、光学薄膜等高端产品将成为市场规模扩张的核心驱动力，传统包装膜增量有限，拥有高端技术储备、产业链配套及优质客户资源的企业将充分受益行业结构性发展机遇。 ... 4、BOPET薄膜行业政策影响 国内多项产业政策从产能出清、技术攻关、标准规范、外资引导等多维度影响BOPET薄膜行业，《加力推进石化化工行业老旧装置更新改造行动方案》推动高能耗老旧产线改造，加速落后产能淘汰，提升行业集中度；《石化化工行业稳增长工作方案》《精细化工产业创新发展实施方案》将高性能膜材料列为重点攻关对象，支持光学、新能源配套BOPET功能膜技术突破与原料改性升级；《鼓励外商投资产业目录（2025年版）》鼓励外资投向功能性聚酯薄膜领域，助力行业高端化、绿色化转型；而GB/T13542.4‑2024绝缘聚酯薄膜国家标准抬高产品性能准入门槛，倒逼企业提升产品质量与制造水平，整体政策环境引导行业告别低端价格内卷，推动行业向高端功能膜国产替代、智能化绿色制造方向发展，利好具备技术与规模优势的龙头企业。 ... 5、BOPET薄膜行业发展趋势 （1）产品结构高端化，加速进口替代 传统普通包装BOPET薄膜产能过剩、价格竞争激烈，行业增长重心逐步转向高附加值功能性薄膜赛道。光伏背板膜、MLCC电容膜、光学基膜、锂电铝塑膜外层等高端产品成为研发和扩产重点，国内头部企业持续在低收缩、高透光、耐候绝缘、超薄规格等关键指标上突破，逐步打破海外企业在高端基材领域的垄断，高端BOPET国产化率持续提升，行业由规模扩张转向质量效益发展。 （2）应用场景多元化，新能源赛道拉动增长 BOPET薄膜需求结构持续重构，传统包装市场保持平稳，新能源、电子显示、新型储能成为核心增量来源。光伏装机扩张带动耐紫外、高阻隔背板用BOPET需求上行；动力电池、复合集流体、功率电子器件拉动绝缘类聚酯薄膜需求；OLED、偏光片、汽车窗膜等领域对光学级BOPET的需求稳步释放。下游新兴产业对薄膜性能定制化要求提升，企业配套研发、定向开发的模式逐步普及，产业链协同持续加深。 （3）生产绿色低碳化，循环材料成为主流方向 在双碳政策与全球限塑、可回收法规驱动下，绿色制造与循环产品成为行业长期主线。一方面企业改造产线，降低能耗、提升拉伸工艺效率，推进清洁生产；另一方面PCR再生料、单材质可回收BOPET、减薄轻量化薄膜快速落地，兼顾使用性能与回收属性。未来符合食品接触标准的再生BOPET、低VOC功能涂层薄膜会持续放量，具备循环材料稳定供给、低碳生产能力的企业，将在国内外市场竞争中建立差异化优势。

headline: [隆众聚焦]：地缘政治反复扰动心态，BOPP行业亏损收窄但扭亏仍难_热点聚焦_塑料制品 - 隆众资讯
summary_text: 导语：进入10月上旬，国内BO PP市场在PP原料上行驱动下，价格同步抬升，行业亏损持续修复，但尚未实现扭亏。中东地缘局势反复波动，持续扰动国际原油与石化原料价格，通过产业链自上而下传导，成为10月BOPP成本端最核心的外部变量。当前BOPP行业处于成本强、需求弱、利润缓慢磨底的格局，膜企持续承受上游原料波动带来的盈利压力，短期盈利大幅改善空间受限。 ... 据隆众资讯数据监测，10月8日-10月19日，受原油风险溢价带动，华东PP现货价格自10371元/吨震荡上行，最高触及10889元/吨，后期小幅回落至10775元/吨。PP是BOPP生产最主要原料，占生产成本88-90%，PP价格上行直接拉动BOPP生产成本由11571元/吨上涨至11975元/吨，成本中枢整体抬升404元/吨，成本端维持高位区间运行。 ... 同期BOPP市场报价跟随原料被动上调，从11200元/吨逐步上调至11850元/吨，但成品涨价幅度不及原料成本涨幅。行业毛利润从10月8日-371元/吨的深度亏损，持续修复至10月16日-105元/吨，为阶段内亏损最低点；10月19日利润小幅回落至-125元/吨，毛利率同步由-3.31%收窄至-1.05%。随着BOPP成品价格逐步追涨，行业亏损幅度明显收窄，但全行业依旧维持亏损状态，成本压力仍是压制盈利的核心因素。 ... 本轮成本上行根源在于中东地缘局势的反复拉扯。中东作为全球原油、丙烷核心产区，霍尔木兹海峡承担大量原油外运，冲突消息反复刺激市场，推升原油地缘风险溢价，直接抬升国内油制PP成本，带动PP现货持续走强。地缘消息具备脉冲式特征，冲突紧张阶段，原油快速拉涨，PP成本跟涨；局势短暂缓和时，风险溢价消退，原料价格小幅回调，这也造成近期华东PP价格冲高后小幅回落，BOPP成本同步震荡。但是从下游终端来看，食品包装、胶带等下游终端订单仅维持刚需采购，高价之下客户抵触情绪明显，缺乏集中补货意愿，市场成交放量有限。BOPP膜企难以将原料上涨压力完全向下游转嫁，即便价格持续上调，涨幅依然无法覆盖PP原料带来的新增成本，行业始终无法摆脱亏损。 ... 展望后市，BOPP盈利修复节奏仍将锚定PP原料走势与终端需求变化。成本重心仍将紧盯中东地缘局势变化。地缘冲突具备突发性、反复性，一旦局势再度紧张，原油风险溢价会快速回归，PP与BOPP成本将再度走高，行业亏损存在再度扩大风险；若冲突阶段性降温，原油溢价回落，成本压力减轻，叠加下游旺季订单释放，BOPP行业存在扭亏可能性。但如果PP继续维持高位震荡，而下游需求无实质性回暖，BOPP利润或将维持小幅波动，深度修复难度较大。 ... 短期来看，BOPP行业大概率还是窄幅调整、亏损磨底的状态。地缘局势带来的成本波动仍是影响盈利的第一变量，而需求真正回暖才是利润反转的关键信号。BOPP企业要持续跟踪原油和PP原料走势，谨慎控制备货，同时密切关注下游订单释放节奏。

headline: PETG薄膜首个国标，潍坊企业主导制定_腾讯新闻
summary_text: 2026 ... 10-09 1 ... 发布于山东 ... 近日，位于潍坊综合保税区的山东圣和薄膜新材料有限公司（以下简称圣和薄膜）主导制定的国家标准《GB/T48041-2026多二元醇共聚聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯(PETG)薄膜通用技术要求》，经国家市场监督管理总局、国家标准化管理委员会正式批准发布。该标准作为我国首个PETG薄膜通用技术要求推荐性国家标准，将于2027年2月1日起实施。 据了解，PETG是一种环保型新材料，市场需求量大，可回收循环利用，无增塑剂迁移风险，广泛应用于瓶身标签、身份证护卡膜、建筑材料覆膜等关系国计民生的材料领域。长期以来，国内PETG薄膜缺乏统一的国家标准，新国标首次从国家层面明确了PETG薄膜的术语定义、产品分类、技术要求、试验方法、检验规则等全流程规范，对拉伸强度、断裂伸长率、热收缩率、雾度、透光率等关键指标提出具体限定，结束了行业“无标可依”的局面。 圣和薄膜用14年技术沉淀，攻克15项关键技术难题并获授权国家发明专利，将高性能双向拉伸聚酯热收缩薄膜的工艺技术和产品性能经验写入国家标准。

headline: Golden Week Restocking and Supply Disruptions Support China's BOPET Prices
summary_text: China's BOPET film market firmed into mid-September as several Asian producers operated below normal rates amid maintenance and feedstock disruptions. A Liaoning producer halted multiple lines, while facilities in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Bangladesh faced reduced rates or force majeure tied to energy shortages. Despite these constraints, China's BOPET exports rose year-on-year in August on recovering overseas demand and pre-holiday restocking, though anti-dumping duties continue to cap returns. Elevated PTA and PET chip costs provided a firm floor under BOPET prices. Meanwhile, Sidi Ke's major high-end functional BOPET base film investment signals a longer-term push to reduce import dependence, even as the commodity-grade segment remains structurally oversupplied. ... headline: BOPET film plants caught between soaring feedstock costs and weak demand | CCFGroup
summary_text: ## BOPET film plants caught between soaring feedstock costs and weak demand Amber Insight | Time: Sep 18 2026 2:10PM Middle East conflicts have driven crude oil above $100/bbl, pushing PTA, MEG and PET fiber chip prices to new highs while BOPET film prices lag behind. Film margins have fallen to yearly lows of -289 yuan/mt (chip method) and -387 yuan/mt (direct melt). With weak downstream demand, feedstock prices remain the key variable. Further conflict escalation would keep margins under pressure, while easing tensions could lower costs and support a profitability recovery. ... This round of upstream feedstock prices and BOPET prices began recovering in July. As of Sep 16, PTA spot negotiations ranged at 7,300–7,550 yuan/mt, MEG spot transactions prices for this week and next week were around 7,060–7,440 yuan/mt, and semi-dull and bright chips were around 8,800–9,000 yuan/mt. It can be seen that feedstock prices have all hit new highs this round, while film prices have yet to hit new highs. On Sep 17, 12μm BOPET printing film was mostly traded at around 10,210–10,510 yuan/mt, compared with the previous April high of around 10,410–11,010 yuan/mt. In mid-to-late August, as the downstream flexible packaging sector gradually recovered, trading sentiment improved somewhat, with downstream buyers making replenishments at around 9,010–9,210 yuan/mt. Subsequently, entering September, feedstock gains accelerated. Film producers, on the one hand, faced continuously escalating costs and had to raise film prices; on the other hand, downstream film buyers found it difficult to accept the cost-driven price increases, and trading sentiment cooled. It can be seen that after BOPET profitability recovered slightly in mid-to-late August, it was continuously compressed in September by the strong rise in feedstock costs. As of September 16, the average profit for the chip method and direct melt method this week stood at -289 yuan/mt and -387 yuan/mt, respectively, down 200 yuan/mt and 237 yuan/mt from the August average. Profits are now near this year's lows, and film producers have limited room for further concessions. At present, with demand relatively weak, feedstock prices are the biggest variable. If the conflict continues or escalates and crude oil, PTA, and MEG prices remain strong, film producers are unlikely to have any profit margin. If the Strait issue is brought under control and feedstock declines drive downstream replenishment, BOPET prices may weaken in tandem while film makers' profitability could recover.

headline: 【市场聚焦】聚丙烯：基本面现状及展望_新浪财经_新浪网
summary_text: 近期 PP期货价格走强，并非终端需求全面回暖催生的趋势行情，而是原料成本抬升、装置阶段性减产、产业链库存低位叠加传统旺季前置预期共同形成的共振行情。需要警惕的是，下游制品端订单并未出现整体性复苏，持续走高的原料价格已经开始压制下游接货意愿，这一轮行情本质是预期交易占主导，实体需求的支撑力度偏弱。 ... 成本端是本轮行情启动的源头。中东地区地缘局势反复扰动原油与丙烷价格，国际原油价格重心抬升，直接抬高油制PP的生产成本；PDH工艺生产线受丙烷涨价冲击更为明显，不少PDH企业陷入持续亏损状态，主动下调生产负荷甚至临时停车，进一步压缩国内PP 商品供应量。OPEC+持续执行减产协议，原油价格下方支撑稳固，原料涨价沿着石化产业链向下传导，国内石化企业出厂报价同步上调，期货盘面率先兑现原料涨价预期。 ... 供应端呈现阶段性收缩特征。前期油制、PDH装置集中安排检修，月度商品料产出同比回落，虽然8月起部分设备陆续重启，但复产进度慢于市场前期预判，行业整体开工水平依旧低于往年同期。拉丝料作为市场主流流通规格，排产占比偏低，现货市场可流通货源偏紧。与此同时，石化厂库、社会贸易库存同步去化，整体库存处在近年相对低位。库存偏低意味着现货缓冲空间有限，一旦贸易商或者下游出现阶段性补库动作，很容易带动现货与期货同步走强。进口货源方面，海外原料成本抬升叠加远洋航运扰动，到港增量有限，很难快速填补国内货源缺口。 ... 需求端呈现明显结构性分化，整体偏弱，但局部存在季节性亮点。进入9月，塑编、BOPP薄膜、薄壁注塑等行业存在传统旺季备货预期，电商包装、食品包装订单有小幅回暖，带动下游工厂开工小幅抬升。不过地产配套管材、汽车改性料板块需求依旧疲弱，终端整体订单规模没有出现实质性改善。价格持续上行之后，下游制品企业成本传导受阻，加工利润被持续挤压，采购策略转向按需采购、随用随拿，大规模囤货意愿不强，这也是本轮上涨过程现货成交始终偏弱的核心矛盾。简单来说，市场博弈的是旺季预期，而不是已经落地的强需求。 ... 中期基准情景：PP维持区间震荡，向上突破空间有限。假设中东地缘摩擦不再进一步升级，原油维持高位震荡，不再出现突发性大幅拉升；国内检修装置按既定计划逐步复产，四季度新增产能有序投产，供应端压力缓慢释放。需求层面，9月塑编、包装行业迎来季节性改善，但回暖力度温和，不足以形成持续拉动，地产链相关需求继续维持弱势。库存由持续去库转为小幅累积，基差逐步收敛，期现回归。在此情景下，PP期货很难走出单边持续上涨行情，价格重心维持区间震荡。上方受新增产能投放、下游对高价原料抵触压制，下方依托原油成本与低位库存形成支撑。行情跟踪重点，需要关注下游成品订单持续性、装置复产进度以及原油价格波动。 ... 中期悲观情景：盘面高位回落，价格重心下移。触发条件包括中东局势缓和，原油前期积累的地缘溢价快速消退；国内检修装置集中复产叠加四季度新产能顺利投产，市场供应集中释放；旺季需求不及市场预期，下游备货力度偏弱，塑编、膜材开工再度回落，终端订单持续走弱。多重利空共振下，产业链进入累库周期，贸易商出货压力加大，现货报价松动，带动期货回调。地产、消费若继续走弱，会进一步拖累注塑、管材等长期需求。该情景下，成本支撑下移叠加供需转向宽松，行情由强转弱，下跌幅度取决于库存累积速度以及下游贸易商止损抛压情况。 ... 本轮PP上涨由成本与低库存共振驱动，但基本面内生需求偏弱，行情稳定性不强。基准情景下中期行情以区间震荡为主，交易主线从持续上涨转向旺季基本面验证；悲观情景下，则需要警惕旺季预期落空叠加供应放量带来的回调风险。

headline: [隆众聚焦]：产能扩张与结构优化并进，中国BOPP行业良性发展任重道远_热点聚焦_首页 - 隆众资讯
summary_text: 【导语】：近年来，国内BOPP行业在规模扩张与结构演进中迎来深刻变局。产能持续攀升、自给率突破120%、产业链协同配套逐步成熟；进口萎缩与出口增长常态化，进一步重塑市场格局。然而规模跨越的背后，同质化竞争加剧、高端产品依赖进口、区域配套不均等结构性矛盾依然突出。未来，国内BOPP扩能步伐不减，企业竞争更趋激烈，机遇与挑战并存，中国BOPP行业良性发展任重道远。 ... 我国BOPP行业产能长期保持持续扩张，目前我国已经成为全球最大的BOPP生产国。从近十年走势来看，国内BOPP产能由2017年576万吨逐年稳步攀升，2025年产能突破840万吨，2026年预计产能达到922万吨，十年间产能实现大幅增长。相较于产能高速扩张，国内BOPP产量虽保持缓慢上行趋势，但增长幅度明显滞后于产能增速，行业产能过剩格局长期延续，供给端增量压力持续偏大。伴随国内BOPP自给供应能力不断增强，BOPP产品出口规模逐年扩大，国内产能除满足国内软包装消费市场需求外，富余产能持续向海外市场释放，后期随着新增产能不断落地投产，行业市场竞争或将进一步加剧。 ... 二 ... BOPP行业国产自给率达 ... 122 ... 进口依存度持续下滑至 1.4 ... BOPP ... ） ... 近年来，在国内经济保持持续增长、居民消费能力稳步提升的大背景下，日用包装等终端消费需求不断释放，为BOPP产业提供了坚实的内需基础。受益于此，BOPP下游实际消费量始终保持良性增长势头，其消费规模从2027年的310万吨增长至2026年的379万吨，增幅达到22.26%，反映出国内下游包装领域对BOPP材料的需求韧性与扩张潜力。与此同时，随着国内BOPP行业产能持续释放，新增产线陆续投产，国产供应能力显著增强，行业自给率逐年走高，截至2026年已攀升至122%的水平。 ... 在这一格局演变过程中，我国BOPP进口量与进口依存度呈现出长期下行的趋势，进口依存度由2017年的3.6%持续回落至目前的1.4%，对外依赖程度显著降低，表明国产BOPP产品在常规应用领域已具备充分的替代能力。整体而言，目前国内普通包装级BOPP已实现高度自给自足，进口产品在市场中的份额被持续压缩，现阶段仅存的少量进口需求主要集中于高端功能性薄膜产品，这类产品因技术门槛较高、国内短期内尚难以完全替代，仍保留一定的进口空间。面向未来，随着国内富余产能的持续累积，过剩产量将越来越多地依赖出口渠道进行消化，出口市场拓展将成为缓解国内BOPP供需压力的关键路径。 ... BOPP企业 ... 化 ... 一体化水平提高 ... 产业链配套进程加快 当前国内BOPP行业产能过剩问题突出，市场供给充裕导致行业竞争压力持续加大。在此背景下，头部BOPP生产企业加速推进产业结构升级，规模化、一体化发展已经成为行业重要发展方向。从国内企业布局趋势来看，产业链配套主要分化为两大路径：一类向上游延伸，配套建设聚丙烯原料产能，打造“PP‑BOPP”一体化项目，以此降低原料采购成本，规避原料价格波动带来的经营风险；另一类向下游拓展，布局胶带、软包装等深加工环节，构建“BOPP‑胶带”产业链，消化自身薄膜产能，提升产品附加值。 截止2026年8月底，中国BOPP行业共有114家生产企业，合计产能达864万吨，已形成以基材产能为核心、上下游就近配套协同的成熟产业格局。从产业链分工维度来看，上游配套企业共6家，主要配套原料PP，有效降低原料物流成本；下游配套企业共13家，以胶带母卷、软包装复合厂及胶粘制品加工企业为主体，依托就近采购BOPP基膜，显著缩短供应链周转周期。在地域布局上，产业集群效应十分显著，基材工厂广泛分布在江苏、浙江、广东、山东、安徽、福建、湖北、四川等东部沿海及中部省份，福融新材料、金田塑业等头部基材企业采取多基地布局模式，在全国多点建厂，形成了覆盖广泛的跨区域基材供给；配套企业的区域分布则与基材产能高度重合，进一步强化了产业链上下游的空间协同效应。 ... 在这一成熟格局之下，BOPP行业也暴露出明显的结构性分化问题。基材端产能相对集中、同质化竞争激烈，而下游胶粘、包装深加工企业数量持续扩容，对高品质、定制化BOPP薄膜的需求不断提升，供需之间的结构性错配日益突出；与此同时，部分基材产区周边下游深加工企业数量偏少，区域上下游配套密度不均衡，导致产品增加了流通成本，削弱了区域内的协同效率。 ... 据隆众资讯数据监测，未来几年国内BOPP行业计划新增投产规模达50万吨以上，综合考虑新装置可能推迟投产以及老旧产能逐步淘汰等现实因素，预计到2030年我国BOPP总产能将突破970万吨/年。随着新扩产能的持续释放，国产供应量不断加大，BOPP行业自给率将在此前122%的基础上继续攀升，进口货源将在更大程度上被国产产品所替代。从当前进口结构来看，我国BOPP进口量已呈长期萎缩态势，而出口增长则成为常态化。 ... 在此背景下，中国BOPP行业正处在产能过剩、同质化竞争加剧、原料价格波动频繁等多重挑战之下，行业利润空间持续承压。未来发展中，企业一方面需主动进行结构性调整，加速向高端化、功能化、绿色化转型发展；另一方面把握东南亚海外包装扩容以及国内生鲜冷链、预制菜等新兴领域带来的特种膜增量需求；同时依托国产宽幅高速生产线普及等工艺升级契机，加快高端产品的国产替代步伐，以此破解同质化困局，打开行业长期成长空间。

headline: 双星新材2026年半年报：优化产品结构，业绩实现扭亏_新浪财经_新浪网
summary_text: 蓝鲸新闻8月25日讯，8月24日，双星新材(002585.SZ)公布2026年中报，公司依托光学材料、新能源材料及聚酯功能膜等核心业务板块，通过优化产品结构、深耕高端细分市场及强化成本管控，成功实现扭亏为盈，经营基本面显著改善；同时，经营活动现金流大幅转正，显示盈利质量与运营效率同步提升。 财报数据显示，报告期公司实现营业收入27.29亿元，同比增长3.89%；归母净利润 0.46亿元，上年同期亏损1.49亿元，实现扭亏为盈；扣非净利润0.06亿元，上年同期亏损1.73亿元，同样实现扭亏。经营活动产生的现金流量净额为5.81亿元，较上年同期的-2.80亿元大幅改善。公司营收保持稳健增长，利润端由亏转盈，且经营性现金流充沛，反映出主业盈利能力修复及营运资金管理能力增强。 从业务结构看，光学材料膜是公司的核心收入来源，报告期内实现营收12.23亿元，占比44.82%，同比增长3.35%，毛利率为8.74%，同比提升3.50个百分点；聚酯功能膜实现营收10.24亿元，占比37.54%，毛利率为5.35%，同比大幅提升18.05个百分点，主要得益于同质化产品销量下降带来的成本优化。新能源材料膜营收规模较小，仅为161.39万元，但毛利率达到29.96%。 ... 业绩扭亏的主要原因在于：一是公司主动规避低端市场恶性竞争，聚焦高附加值的光学材料及功能性薄膜，推动产品结构优化，带动整体毛利率回升；二是通过精细化成本管控，营业成本同比下降5.47%，降幅高于营收增幅；三是非经常性损益贡献较大，包括政府补助2342万元及金融资产公允价值变动收益2200万元，合计非经常性损益达3991万元，对当期利润形成重要支撑。 当前BOPET行业处于深度结构调整期，低端产能过剩与高端供给不足并存。随着消费电子、新能源汽车及光伏等下游应用领域需求稳步增长，以及国产替代进程加速，高性能聚酯薄膜市场空间广阔。公司凭借“基材+膜片”全产业链优势，在光学基材、MLCC离型膜及复合集流体等高端领域持续突破，有望受益于行业格局优化。然而，公司仍面临原材料价格波动、行业竞争加剧及新项目收益不及预期等风险。后续需重点关注光学材料及新能源高端产品的放量进度、原材料成本传导机制以及非经常性损益对利润影响的可持续性。

headline: Firsta Group validates ILC-BOPP film for 150°C use
summary_text: -BOPP combines ... ial ... of the polypropylene ... with application of functional coating during production. ... The company’s ILC-BOPP production line was built with Brückner. Credit: Firsta Group/ Brückner. Firsta Group has concluded validation tests on a high-barrier in-line coated biaxially oriented polypropylene (ILC-BOPP) coated base film developed in-house, with performance measures reaching the required level at 150°C. The outcome represents a further stage in the development of ILC-BOPP for uses that involve higher operating temperatures. The company’s ILC-BOPP production line was built with Brückner. According to Firsta, it is the first industrial-scale ILC-BOPP line of this type in China and a step in bringing inline coating technology into wider use in the domestic market. In the standard offline method, film is produced first and coated in a separate process. By contrast, ILC-BOPP combines biaxial orientation of the polypropylene substrate with application of the functional coating during production. Firsta said this setup is meant to streamline manufacturing while supporting the development of films with greater heat resistance, barrier properties and other functions. The company has built a functional-film production platform spanning BOPP, BOPET, coating, metallisation and masterbatch. Its high-barrier ILC-BOPP films are already being produced in batches for applications such as electronic component protection; food, pharmaceutical and medical packaging; and new energy materials. The newly validated temperature-resistant ILC-BOPP base film is under development for uses that require both heat resistance and barrier performance. Firsta said it offers another polypropylene-based material option for packaging and functional-film applications with stricter requirements. The company will keep moving the temperature-resistant ILC-BOPP technology towards industrial-scale production and continue work on functional films designed for applications needing stronger barrier and thermal performance. Brückner Group global electrical director Thomas said: “As part of our cooperation with Firsta Group, we redesigned and manufactured a customised Brückner coating system based on Firsta’s specific requirements and the needs of the global market. “By integrating the coating process into the production line, the system significantly reduces energy consumption and enables zero VOC [volatile organic compounds] emissions.”

headline: 国风新材：上半年营收11.68亿元 同比增长13.96%_新浪财经_新浪网
summary_text: 上证报中国证券网讯 国风新材 8月19日发布2026年半年报。报告期内，公司实现营业收入11.68亿元，同比增长13.96%，主业规模稳步扩容；同时实现归母净利润、扣非净利润同比大幅减亏，彻底扭转前期亏损扩大态势，叠加外贸业务高增、高端产能落地、产业并购推进，公司高质量发展动能持续释放。 外贸业务强势爆发，多板块多点开花。公司内外市场双向突破，出口业务成为核心增长极。BOPP、BOPET功能薄膜、复合预涂膜出口销量快速增长，绿色木塑材料出口及线上交易额大幅提升。细分赛道成果突出，汽车材料成功切入头部车企供应链，多款产品通过上汽、蔚来、领途认证并批量供货；聚酰亚胺薄膜销量持续扩容，子公司国风木塑产量、利润双双大幅增长，新兴业务增量势能持续释放。 ... 高端产能加速落地，产品结构持续升级。公司持续加码技术创新与项目建设，夯实长期成长基底。依托升级的研发体系与新建光电新材料研发平台，公司创新成果持续落地，专利、省级新产品申报数量稳步提升，技术壁垒不断加固。重点项目进展超预期，年产10亿平米光学级聚酯基膜项目G1线进入精细调试阶段、G2线稳步安装，安庆新能源材料项目完成试车并启动客户审核，高端光学、新能源新材料产能即将释放，助力公司切入高景气赛道。 ... 改革赋能提效，并购整合完善产业链。国企改革持续深化，公司完成顶层战略规划迭代，通过扁平化机构优化、精益管理升级、研发市场协同机制改革，大幅激活内部经营活力、提升运营效率。资本运作同步提速，太湖金张科技并购重组有序推进，且双方已提前开展产业协同，打通基膜到精密功能涂布完整产业链，攻坚偏光片离型膜、柔性封装材料等国产替代领域，补齐高端新材料产业链短板，打开中长期成长空间。（叶菲）

headline: 需求结构分化 我国BOPP电容膜行业产能与效率同步升级 国内龙头正逐步主导高端市场_新浪财经_新浪网
summary_text: 一、BOPP电容膜是薄膜电容器核心介质材料，占电容成本的40%–50% BOPP电容膜（电工级双向拉伸聚丙烯薄膜）是薄膜电容器唯一核心介质，占电容器总成本 40%~50%，决定电容耐压、耐温、寿命、能量密度。 数据来源：观研天下数据中心整理 二、我国BOPP电容膜行业处第三轮扩能周期，装置宽度向5.8米、6.2米宽幅线集中 根据观研报告网发布的《中国BOPP电容膜行业现状深度分析与发展前景预测报告（2026-2033年）》显示，我国BOPP电容膜行业自1985年从德国布鲁克纳引进首条生产线起步，已跨越四十余年发展历程，经历了从进口依赖到全球最大制造国的产业跃迁。 当前，我国BOPP电容膜行业正处于力度最强的第三轮扩能周期，截至2025年8月国内已有20家生产企业、63条产线，总产能达16.3万吨，2025年前8个月即新增7条产线；据统计，2027年前仍有20余条产线待投产，行业产能即将突破20万吨。从扩能节奏看，本轮周期年均新增产线6.7条，远超此前两轮的3.2条和2.75条，且装置宽度向5.8米、6.2米宽幅线集中，两者合计占比达60%，产能与效率同步升级。 中国 B O PP电容膜新增投产情况 企业名称 计划条数 预计投产时间 百正电子 1 2026 年下半年 扬州博恒 1 2025 年底 华生科技 2 2026 年 南洋华诚 4 2025-2026 年 广东创富 4 2026 年及以后 泉州嘉德利 1 —— 厦门嘉德利 3 厦门中仑 2 2025-2026 年 佛山达孚 2026 年 湖北龙辰 2 2025-2026 年 安徽龙辰 2026 年 江苏双凯 2026 年 江苏恒创 2026 年 合计 ... 三、BOPP电容膜核心需求来自四大高景气赛道，行业结构性分化格局持续 BOPP电容膜核心需求来自四大高景气赛道： 一是新能源汽车。800V高压平台与SiC电控加速普及，整车高压高频升级，带动车载OBC、主逆变器、DC/DC等电控部件电容用量大幅提升，刚需1.2–2.5μm超薄、125℃耐高温高端BOPP膜，是行业核心增长引擎。 二是光伏储能。薄膜电容凭借低损耗、长寿命、自愈性强的优势，是逆变器、储能PCS滤波环节的核心优选器件。 三是特高压及电网。柔直换流阀、SVG等电网核心设备高度依赖高压薄膜电容，单条±800kV特高压线路需配套120吨电容膜。国内新型电力系统、输电改造工程持续落地，为高压特种电容膜提供长期稳健需求。 四是AI算力数据中心。高功耗AI服务器普及800V HVDC高压直流架构，高压母线需大量薄膜电容稳压滤波，设备电容用量大幅提升，为高端BOPP电容膜开辟全新增量市场。 ... 四大赛道同步扩容，叠加下游设备高压、高频、小型化迭代，高端超薄耐高温电容膜持续紧缺、量价向好；而中低端常规膜需求疲软，行业结构性分化格局持续。 ... 超薄化 ... BOPP 电容膜正朝着超薄化方向发展，厚度从传统的 6-8μm 向 3μm 以下迈进。超薄电容膜在新能源汽车电驱系统等领域优势显著，它能有效降低电容器的体积和重量，提升能量密度，使新能源汽车的电驱系统更加紧凑高效。创富新材已成功实现 2μm 产品量产，供应给华为、比亚迪等头部企业，有力推动了相关产业的技术升级。 ... 通过聚丙烯和环烯烃聚合物（COC）的复配技术，BOPP 电容膜的耐高温性能和力学性能得到显著增强。复配后的材料可开发出 120℃以上耐温产品，满足新能源发电领域中光伏逆变器、风电变流器等在高温环境下的使用需求。这种复合化技术还能改善薄膜的介电性能，提升其在高频环境下的稳定性，为开发高性能电容膜开辟了新路径。 ... 绿色生产技术在 BOPP 电容膜生产中日益受到重视。余热回收系统可将生产过程中的废热进行回收再利用，用于预热原料或其他工序，降低能源消耗。部分企业采用绿电作为生产能源，从源头减少碳排放。2024 年，采用绿色工艺生产的 BOPP 电容膜产品占比达 31.5% ，随着技术的发展和环保意识的增强，这一比例有望在 2025 年提升至 45%，推动行业向绿色可持续方向发展。 ... 四、三重壁垒锁定BOPP电容膜行业供给刚性，国内龙头正逐步主导高端市场 BOPP电容膜行业高端产能扩容极难，主要由于三重核心壁垒高筑：设备端依赖德国布鲁克纳6.4米宽幅磁悬浮同步拉伸产线，单条产线投资高达2–3亿元，设备交付周期超18个月，仅少数头部企业具备采购与量产运营能力；工艺端要求严苛，超薄膜厚度偏差需控制在2%以内，同时需实现125℃长效耐温、高击穿场强等核心性能，新产线从投产到良率稳定至85%以上，需耗时1–2年打磨；认证端周期漫长，车规AEC-Q200、光伏TUV/UL、电网等核心认证周期长达18–24个月，新玩家难以快速切入优质核心供应链。 数据来源：观研天下数据中心整理 高壁垒加持下，行业头部集中度持续提升，2025年末国内高端电容膜产能CR3超50%，竞争格局高度清晰。 其中，龙辰科技 2025年末BOPP基膜产能占有率17%，行业排名第一，其依托9条产线实现2.7–12μm全规格覆盖，2.0μm超薄产品量产工艺成熟，客户资源稳定优质；中仑新材大力布局高端产能，总投资25亿元规划9条高端产线，首条6.4米宽幅磁悬浮同步拉伸产线已于2025年11月投产，第二条产线预计2026年下半年落地，技术对标日系东丽，产品已通过法拉电子等头部客户送样验证，成功切入宁德时代、比亚迪核心供应链；大东南聚焦特高压高端赛道，相关产品缺口超50%，产能利用率高达96.67%，全新产线将于2026年6月投产，持续释放高端产能增量。 伴随国内企业技术突破与产能落地，进口替代进程全面加速，东丽、三菱等海外厂商在高端市场的份额持续收窄，国产头部企业正逐步主导高端BOPP电容膜市场。 ... 产能与扩产规划 核心客户 龙辰科技 2025年末BOPP基膜产能占有率17%，行业排名第一 产品厚度覆盖2.7–12μm全规格；国家级专精特新“小巨人”，拥有142项专利，形成6项自主研发核心技术 截至2025年末共9条基膜产线投产，年产能约2.4万吨 温州正泰电容器、青岛诚汶电子等，客户粘性强 嘉德利 2024年电容器用聚丙烯薄膜销售额全球第二（11.7%）、国内第一（16.4%） 已实现1.9μm超薄膜、125°C超耐温膜等标志性产品规模化量产；国家级专精特新“小巨人” 已投产8条BOPP电工膜产线（其中4条为同步拉伸工艺），3条在建；IPO计划融资7.25亿元 法拉电子、鹰峰电子、TDK、KEMET等，前五大客户收入占比六成 中仑新材 全球BOPA膜材龙头跨界切入BOPP电容膜赛道；首条6.4米宽幅磁悬浮同步拉伸产线已投产 产品聚焦高端超薄电容膜与复合集流体基膜；2–4μm超薄膜填补国产化产能缺口；掌握全球少数三种双向拉伸工艺 规划9条产线，总投资25亿元；首条产线2025年11月已投产，第二条预计2026年下半年投产 法拉电子、汇川联合动力、南通江海等；此前PHA锂电膜已进入比亚迪、宁德新能源等供应链 铜峰电子 深耕电容薄膜领域逾三十年，国内老牌BOPP电容膜厂商 6条聚丙烯薄膜生产线，产品厚度2.2–18μm；六线专门面向新能源汽车用超薄薄膜（2.0–3.4μm） 年产各类聚丙烯薄膜1.8万吨；拟投资3.5亿元引进两条超薄型薄膜生产线 覆盖新能源汽车、光伏风电、特高压等领域 ... 大 ... 容 ... 参与 ... headline: 中仑新材(301565.SZ)：计划投资25亿元建设新能源膜材项目
summary_text: 中 ... 新 ... +0 ... 格隆汇8月5日丨中仑新材(301565.SZ)在投资者关系中表示，有被问到:公司最新的产品矩阵和产能布局情况？ 答:公司产品涵盖新能源膜材、功能性膜材、生物基可降解膜材及高性能聚酰胺材料，赋能下游多个行业。其中，新能源膜材包含运用于软包锂电池和固态电池铝塑膜的新能源BOPA膜材、以及运用于薄膜电容器和复合集流体的BOPP新能源膜材；功能性膜材主要为具备较高阻氧性、耐穿刺、较高拉伸强度的双向拉伸聚酰胺膜材（BOPA膜材），生物基可降解膜材为在一定条件下可实现完全降解的双向拉伸聚乳酸膜材（BOPLA膜材）。 新能源膜材方面，公司计划投资25亿元建设新能源膜材项目，旨在进一步丰富公司的“高精尖”产品矩阵，提升行业竞争力，项目分期建设，其中一期项目规划两条产线，目前处于产品市场推广及客户储备阶段，首条产线已于2025年11月投产，第二条产线预计于2026年投产。 功能性BOPA膜材方面，公司在国内建有两个生产基地，分别位于厦门、泉州，截至目前，拥有15条生产线，国内总产能为16.50万吨/年，待规划产能（共规划16条产线）全部达产后，国内总产能将突破18.50万吨/年，产能规模位居全球首位；海外建有一个膜材生产基地，位于印尼西爪哇省，截至目前，印尼长塑一期、二期共规划4条生产线，达产后将为公司在海外带来9万吨/年产能增量，可深度服务东南亚及周边地区市场，进一步提升公司在全球膜材领域的供应能力与市场渗透率。届时，公司国内外总产能预计将为27.50万吨/年，可更好地发挥规模优势，进一步增强综合竞争力，为满足市场需求、扩大市场份额提供了有力保障。生物基可降解膜材方面，公司已成功攻克生物基可降解膜材生产的技术瓶颈并成功将产品产业化。在全球材料市场向环保化发展的大趋势下，伴随着国内可降解材料环保政策的逐步实施，生物基可降解膜材将迎来更大的市场空间，公司作为全球极少数能够批量生产膜材的企业，有望优先受益于未来行业成长。 ... 高性能聚酰胺材料方面，公司现有产能约14.50万吨/年，至2027年，高性能聚酰胺材料产业化项目全部建成后，将带来21万吨的产能增量（其中，IPO募投项目产能14万吨，自有资金建设项目产能7万吨），全部达产后，总产能35.50万吨/年，项目产能优先保障公司新增BOPA产能对原材料的需求，进一步凸显产业链一体化优势，进一步带动成本优势加原材料端产品创新，促进下游膜材的新产品开发及性能优化，更好地实现协同创新。

headline: 德冠新材：高端功能性BOPP薄膜目前仍存在供给缺口
summary_text: 德冠 ... 功能 ... BOPP ... 目前仍存在供给 ... 口 ... 0 ... 08-04 ... 6:27:03 ... 来源：同花顺iNews 同花顺（300033）金融研究中心08月04日讯，有投资者向德冠新材（001378）提问， 看到最近乐庭在平江投资10亿功能性bopp薄膜，号称填补华南高端薄膜市场。公司对这个项目有所了解吗？是不是直接形成竞争？感觉高端市场也很卷。 公司回答表示，尊敬的投资者，您好！从行业格局来看，高端功能性BOPP薄膜目前仍存在供给缺口，高端产品的国产化替代依然是行业未来发展的重要方向。公司秉持差异化发展路径，以“功能化、高端化、环保化”为创新导向开拓产品与市场，作为国内领先的薄膜新材料系统解决方案供应商，公司已成为众多知名品牌的信赖之选，产品终端市场广阔且分布广泛，覆盖乳制品、酒类饮料、日化用品、智能手机与可穿戴设备、新能源（850101）电池等众多领域。公司持续加大研发投入，截至2026年3月31日，专利总数已达203项，公司核心产品无胶膜已迭代升级至第十代，扩展至20多项发明专利保护，更好地满足了下游客户高性能、轻量化和高速度的生产需求。同时，公司正全面推进“膜材料（884213）+”的差异化战略。公司始终保持对行业竞争格局的敏锐洞察，有信心依托深厚的技术积累、完善的研发体系与稳健的产能布局，在高端功能性薄膜领域持续巩固竞争优势。感谢您对公司的关注。

headline: AL Circle analysis: Germany’s aluminium trade surplus, Novelis’ US expansion, Asia’s EV demand & India’s underutilised downstream capacity
summary_text: Aluminium’s next growth phase is increasingly being shaped by downstream processing, supply-chain resilience and demand from specialised applications. Key takeaways - Track commissioning milestones: Novelis’ Bay Minette project could reshape regional supply as production ramps up; buyers should follow actual output, not just announced capacity. - Build supply alternatives: The Oswego disruption shows the value of qualifying backup suppliers before an unexpected production stoppage. - Secure suitable scrap: Recycling investments make regional scrap availability, quality and procurement costs increasingly important to project economics.

headline: All eyes on ‘high stakes’ North America trade talks as US aluminum sector begins Q4
summary_text: US aluminum industry leaders are closely watching trade talks with Canada and Mexico, as negotiations could lead to major changes in pricing and trade flows. The US decision not to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement trade pact in July has led to intense negotiations between the US and its two largest trading partners. The US is heavily reliant on primary aluminum supply from Canada, and 90% of the aluminum scrap imported to support US manufacturers comes from Canada and Mexico, according to the US-based Aluminum Association trade group. Industry leaders say changes to US trade relations with either country have the potential to significantly revamp the tightly integrated North American aluminum industry. “The [North America] trade talks are very high stakes,” Jake Skelton, CEO of EGA Americas Inc., a subsidiary of aluminum producer Emirates Global Aluminum PJSC, told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, in an interview. “Any kind of reduction to the current tariff rates for either Mexico or Canada will have a profound impact on demand for their aluminum and on US manufacturers.” ... Canada accounted for 60.5% of US primary aluminum imports in 2025, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence’s Global Trade Atlas, a period which included six months of a US 50% tariff on aluminum. Canada diverted some shipments toward European customers in the wake of the new duties, and thesituation fueled record-high prices in US aluminum as well as historically tight supply conditions. “US-Canada trade talks in particular are top of mind,” Duncan Pitchford president of Norsk Hydro ASA’s US aluminum operations, told Platts. “That’s primarily because of the amount of aluminum production in Canada. A changed tariff regime towards Canada could result in changes in metal flow, and changes in pricing, especially the Midwest [Premium].” Platts assessed the spot 99.7% P1020 US Aluminum Transaction Premium at $1.087/pound plus LME cash, delivered Midwest, net 30-day payment terms, on Sept. 28. The assessment, known as the Midwest Premium, is over four times higher than it was at the start of 2025, primarily due to the tariff and the attacks on Middle Eastern producers in the course of a war between Iran and the US and Israel. ... Mexico deal ‘biggest threat’ for some US extruders Other industry leaders, however, said that US negotiations with Mexico could be more consequential for some in the US aluminum sector, especially extruders. “The trade talks with Mexico are going to affect me a lot more than the Canadian ones,” Mark McClelland, president of Texas-based Tower Extrusions LLC, told Platts. “If they lower tariffs on Mexico, non-market economy type metal can find its way into the US. So to me, that’s actually our biggest threat, from an extruder standpoint.” ... In response to US concerns, Mexico published a new aluminum import monitoring system on April 2. “This measure increases traceability requirements for aluminum entering Mexico and supports efforts to address possible third-country transshipment,” the US International Trade Administration said in an April 14 statement.

headline: Novelis Produces First Coil at Greenfield Aluminum Rolling and Recycling Plant in Alabama :: Novelis Inc.
summary_text: # Novelis Produces First Coil at Greenfield Aluminum Rolling and Recycling Plant in Alabama October 07, 2026 10:00am EDT Download as PDF Milestone advances one of the largest new U.S. aluminum manufacturing investments in decades toward commercial shipments in 2027 BAY MINETTE, Ala., Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Novelis Inc., a leading sustainable aluminum solutions provider and the world leader in aluminum rolling and recycling, has produced the first coil on the cold mill at its $5 billion aluminum recycling and rolling plant in Bay Minette. "With the North American market being capacity constrained, this investment will help Novelis meet long-term market demand, strengthen our U.S. manufacturing footprint and increase the use of recycled content in our products." Bay Minette is the first fully integrated aluminum recycling and rolling plant to be built in the United States in more than 40 years. When fully operational, the facility will add 600 kilotonnes of annual rolled aluminum capacity to serve beverage packaging, automotive and specialty product markets. The plant also includes a recycling center that will be capable of processing more than 15 billion used beverage cans annually. All assets at Bay Minette required to commence commercial shipments are currently in the commissioning process. Novelis is working toward customer qualification and commercial shipments, which are on track to begin in the second quarter of 2027. The highly advanced facility is expected to create up to 1,000 new jobs once fully operational.

headline: Aluminum Report - Metal Center News - Solutions for Profitable Distribution
summary_text: An otherwise modest year for nonferrous products was thrown a lifeline by the ongoing push for data centers. Ayear of small demand growth for the aluminum market has been downgraded to one of modest decline. That’s despite the obvious boost being delivered by America’s favorite hero and/or villain, the data center. “We expected some growth, but as the GCC conflict has continued on, we’ve changed our forecast to demand being slightly down for the year. It’s based on economic conditions we are dealing with across the U.S. and all of North America, with high prices pushing down consumer durables,” said Tain Satterlee, an aluminum products analyst for CRU. In September, in conjunction with Steel Market Update’s Steel Summit, CRU also held an Aluminum Summit where officials gathered to discuss the state of the industry. And other than the stagnant demand picture, it has been a remarkably noteworthy one for the nonferrous supply chain, with major developments in pricing, rolling mill supply and the potential for new primary production in the U.S. The Trump tariff regimes, launched in 2025, were more fully felt by industry players this year. Prices of the material have skyrocketed, particularly the Midwest Premium, owing to the 50 percent tariffs. That, in turn, has led to some predictable behavior changes. “From a producer standpoint, the spot market has been more muted than is typically the case,” Satterlee said after the completion of the aluminum event. “With drastic price changes, no one wants to catch the falling price at the wrong end, making a contract and then getting smoked by prices going the wrong way. People working hand to mouth has been the talking point we’ve heard this year.” CRU anticipates the scorching price environment of 2026 will ease considerably in 2027, due to some gains on the supply side around the world. “Globally, supply will be pushed upward by Chinese investments in Indonesia, Angola and Vietnam, which will help bring down the LME price and help reduce the Midwest Premium,” Satterlee said. “With the Midwest premium going down, that will help bolster demand in the U.S.” Demand this year was mixed, a disappointment considering expectations. Automotive was relatively flat, with units in the 15 to 16 million range. The industry is still hopeful the push toward lightweighting will benefit nonferrous material, though the pause on the rush to electric vehicles is a slight hiccup on growth in that market. That’s been a particular annoyance for the aluminum extrusion market. “The transition to EVs is not going the way we planned it. Three years ago we were looking at four billion pounds going into EV markets. The extrusion intensity with battery boxes was very good for us. A lot of people tooled up to do a lot of different parts and those programs were canceled or delayed,” said Jason Weber, president of the Aluminum Extruders Council. There have been some major victims of the delay. “There was significant investment in the supply chain and the OEMs to get at the electrification of powertrains. A lot of money lost, a lot of companies that have gone out of business betting on EVs,” said Scott Ulnick, managing principal at Ducker Carlisle. Of course, the EV slowdown is good news for those companies still connected with ICE programs, Weber added. Another major market, can sheet is typically fairly stable. One change in the coming years is on the supply side, with the U.S. expected to require fewer imports in that space given Aluminum Dynamics’ growing presence and Novelis’ investment at its Bay Minette facility in Alabama, which is still in the long process toward full production. One question surrounding can sheet is in Mexico, where China has maintained a dominant market share position. Given the investments of the U.S. producers, they will undoubtedly want to make inroads into that market, said Paul Williams, head of Aluminum Value Chain for CRU. The softest market has been building and construction, with a number of factors working against it. “U.S. housing starts are weak. Mortgage rates are very high. Consumer sentiment [is weakening]. There’s even a lack of workers to build houses,” Williams said. There is hope the demand increase that failed to materialize in 2026 will instead be pushed ahead another year. “Overall, the macro numbers would say 2025 was a down year and 2026 is as well, though in more recent months we’re starting to see demand pick up, or at least the sentiment is picking up,” Weber said. One source for optimism is the increased potential for reshoring, driven in part by trade policy. With reshoring, overall demand doesn’t need to increase for the nonferrous supply chain to grow. Data centers, of course, have been able to prop up a lot of the industry, even as the boom has been met with increasing public opposition in the last six months. Still, the growth is undeniable. There are currently 4,500 data centers operating in the United States. That number is expected to increase by 60 percent by the end of next year, with 700 of those facilities already under construction and an additional 1,900 planned and identified. There has been a significant shift in their locations. Previously, the vast majority had been situated in urban environments. The next batch will go to more rural sites, which will drive questions on labor availability and power sources, said John Mucci, vice president of sales at Kibar Americas. While steel may have a bigger share in the physical construction of the data centers, the entire aluminum supply chain has and will continue to benefit from their erection. Sheet and extrusion products are used in the building and construction, while foil and extrusions are used in the ample heating and cooling systems required by the structures. Moreover, there’s also the issue of powering these energy-voracious operations. “Aluminum plays an important role in battery storage and the function of them, and also the electrical transmission lines,” he said at the event. The data center surge will have a major effect on foil requirements. It’s estimated there will be an additional 26 million pounds needed on an annual basis. For instance, the cooling systems in a data center have 150 times the cooling capacity of residential applications and 20 times the capacity of warehouses and offices. “The cooling rates are substantially different than anything we’ve experienced on a day-to-day basis,” he said. That will put strain on the U.S. production capacity, particularly in foil and EC wire rod. “Currently a large gap exists between U.S. capacity to build foil products and U.S. apparent demand,” he said. “Packaging, HVAC, consumer durables, all want foil. There’s 475 million pounds on an annual basis that has to be imported to support total demand.” Kibar has done a little bit to alleviate that issue, reopening the idled Fairmont, W.Va., facility it purchased earlier this year. The facility had been a cold-rolled and foil company owned by Novelis that was idled five years earlier. But that’s hardly enough to balance the scales. “Since, 2020, five U.S. foil mills have closed. There’s been some additions since 2023, with one new mill announced focused on battery foil,” said Mucci. “Two of the closed mills have partially restarted, but the focus is on other markets.” Capacity has been an ongoing concern throughout 2026, sparked by two separate fires at Novelis’s Oswego, N.Y., plant a few months apart toward the tail end of 2025. The plant didn’t resume production until the middle of this year. With Aluminum Dynamics still in the ramp-up mode, that left a serious hole in the North American market, one that had to be filled by imports, tariffs be damned. Conversely, import levels should recede next year with the full return of Oswego, the continued growth at ADI and other investments that will have the U.S. market better served by domestics. “That additional production is not going to cover all the demand of the U.S., but it speaks to a sign the tariffs, from a semi standpoint, are making it more attractive to produce the semis in the U.S. From a semi consumption standpoint, ADI and Fairmont getting repurchased, it’s showing companies in the aluminum space are opening up more investments than they have historically. Tariffs are doing part of that as margins are more attractive,” Satterlee said. The biggest investment in the works is actually on the primary side. Century Aluminum and Emirates Global Aluminum continue to move forward on the Inola, Okla., smelter, the first primary aluminum production facility planned in the United States in half a century. The $4 billion project would almost double the country’s primary aluminum production capacity. The operation was dealt a setback a few months back when Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond filed suit to halt construction of the facility. However, the pro-smelter Mike Mazzie subsequently edged out Drummond in the recent Republican primary for the governor’s office in Oklahoma, providing greater optimism the project will eventually go through. “I’m enormously excited. I believe its prospects are good,” said Charles Johnson, president of the Aluminum Association. “The U.S. has been a responsible smelting country. We can smelter responsibly in the U.S. As an industry, I would like to see more smelters in the U.S. But we know what everyone else knows – we have to see the right energy deal. You can do a lot of things, but you have to have energy policy if you want smelters.” ?

headline: South Korea’s aluminium foil imports hit five-year high at 57kt in YTD July 2026 as China drives 96% of new volume
summary_text: South Korea’s aluminium foil market has entered a stronger phase in 2026, with imports reaching their highest level in five years. But the trade data points to a more specific shift beneath the headline growth: most of the additional aluminium foil entering South Korea is coming from China. South Korea imported 57,261.18 tonnes of aluminium foil from the world in YTD July 2026, up 23.94 per cent from 46,201.68 tonnes in YTD July 2025. Imports stood at 50,840.22 tonnes in YTD 2022, 43,145.18 tonnes in YTD 2023 and 47,238.94 tonnes in YTD 2024, before slipping to 46,201.68 tonnes in 2025, as per ITA. The return to growth is clear, but the supplier data reveals where that recovery is coming from. China supplies 92% of South Korea’s aluminium foil imports China supplied 52,751.81 tonnes of aluminium foil to South Korea in YTD July 2026, an increase of 25.32 per cent from 42,093.41 tonnes in YTD July 2025. That lifted China's share of the Korean market from 91.11 per cent to 92.12 per cent in just one year. The difference becomes clearer when the increase is compared in terms of actual volume. South Korea's total aluminium foil imports increased by 11,059.50 tonnes between YTD July 2025 and YTD July 2026. Chinese supplies alone increased by 10,658.40 tonnes. China then increased its shipments 12.53 per cent to 43,737.44 tonnes in YTD 2024. In YTD 2025, Chinese supplies again fell 3.76 per cent to 42,093.41 tonnes. Top aluminium foil exporters to South Korea After China, Thailand remained South Korea’s second-largest supplier in YTD July 2026, but its shipments fell 15.44 per cent to 1,539.94 tonnes from 1,821.20 tonnes in YTD July 2025. Compared with 1,700.11 tonnes in YTD July 2024, Thailand’s supplies were down 9.42 per cent. Japan moved into third place, with shipments rising 60.84 per cent year on year to 987.76 tonnes from 614.14 tonnes. Over two years, supplies increased 89.71 per cent from 520.67 tonnes in YTD July 2024. Germany ranked fourth, supplying 510.95 tonnes in YTD July 2026, up 14.79 per cent from 445.10 tonnes a year earlier. Its shipments more than doubled from 231.32 tonnes in YTD July 2024, recording a 120.88 per cent increase over two years. Slovenia completed the top five in YTD July 2026 with 261.38 tonnes. It replaced Malaysia, which was the fifth-largest supplier in YTD July 2025 with 282.84 tonnes. ... Battery production is adding to aluminium foil demand South Korea's battery industry is one of the areas generating additional aluminium foil requirements. Aluminium foil is used as the cathode current collector in lithium-ion cells, making it an essential component in battery manufacturing. LG Energy Solution began production of 46-series cylindrical batteries at its Ochang plant and had secured an order backlog exceeding 300 GWh for the format by the end of 2025. Samsung SDI also began mass production of 46-series cylindrical batteries at its Cheonan plant in March 2025. The scale of this industry helps explain the potential impact on foil demand. Lotte Aluminium estimates that one GWh of battery capacity requires around 700 tonnes of electric foil. As battery production expands, the associated requirement for foil can therefore increase quickly. The Korean government and industry are continuing to invest in the sector. In September 2026, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy announced a next-generation battery programme involving approximately KRW 400 billion in government R&D spending over five years. Industry participants have also committed around KRW 8 trillion towards R&D and production-facility expansion from 2026 to 2030, creating further requirements for battery materials, including aluminium foil. ... Why China is supplying most of South Korea’s additional aluminium foil China’s lead in South Korea’s aluminium foil market is linked to both product range and supply scale. Korean buyers source several types of foil, including unbacked foil, jumbo rolls, flexible-packaging foil, pharmaceutical foil, capacitor foil and increasingly battery-related material. Chinese producers can supply these different requirements, from price-sensitive packaging and converter-grade jumbo rolls to thin-gauge and battery-related foil, where tighter thickness control, surface condition and consistent quality are required. China also has a large export base, with aluminium foil exports reaching 802,000 tonnes in January-July 2026. For Korean buyers, this combination of product variety, manufacturing scale and availability makes China a practical source across multiple end-use sectors, helping explain its continued dominance in the Korean market.

headline: Aluminum investment across North America and Asia: Who leads reshaping the next phase of growth?
summary_text: Between 2021 and 2026, major projects across North America and Asia have targeted new primary capacity, lower-carbon production, recycled aluminum and higher-value downstream products. But the investment pattern is different: North America is concentrating on recycling, downstream processing and domestic supply resilience, while Asia is expanding across a much broader upstream-to-downstream chain. The result is two distinct models for the next phase of aluminum growth. ... North America: Recycling-led growth with a primary-metal reset North America’s recent investment cycle is centered on recycled metal, flat-rolled products and lower-carbon production. The region is also seeing its first serious attempt in decades to rebuild primary-aluminum capacity. North America is not pursuing primary aluminum volume alone. The projects place recycled aluminum, flat-rolled products (FRP), extruded products, lower-carbon smelting and domestic processing capacity alongside new primary production. That makes the investment cycle more about rebuilding a connected regional supply chain than simply adding smelter tonnes. ... Based on the selected projects, North America has committed around $14.8 billion to aluminum investments since 2021, centered on recycling, flat-rolled products, low-carbon smelting and domestic supply-chain resilience. Asia’s comparable disclosed project pipeline totals about $22.1 billion, reflecting broader investment across alumina refining, primary aluminum, battery foil, rolling, recycling and EV-linked downstream manufacturing; the figure rises to approximately $25 billion when Indonesia’s planned second alumina-refinery phase and smelter are included. While Asia leads in aggregate disclosed investment and upstream integration, North America is strengthening its position through large recycling-and-rolling projects such as Novelis Bay Minette and Steel Dynamics’ Mississippi complex, Québec’s low-carbon AP60 smelter expansion and inert-anode technology, and the proposed Century–EGA primary smelter in Oklahoma. This strategy prioritizes higher-value, lower-carbon aluminum products and a more secure regional supply base rather than competing solely on primary-metal volume. ... Beyond the projects themselves, the US aluminum investment cycle could create opportunities across a much wider domestic industrial ecosystem. The expansion of primary aluminum, recycling, rolling, extrusion and downstream capacity is likely to generate demand not only for aluminum producers but also for companies supplying smelting and casthouse equipment, refractory systems, molten-metal handling solutions, recycling technologies, process automation, industrial gases, casting systems, tooling and specialized downstream manufacturing. Against this backdrop, the following US-based companies, which play significant roles across different segments of the aluminum value chain, could potentially benefit from the investment pipeline as new capacity moves from development to construction, commissioning and full-scale operation.

headline: German aluminium foil exports fall 2.8% in H1 2026 despite higher volume supplied to France: How will H2 unfold? | Mysteel
summary_text: Germany's aluminium foil export market is showing a shift after two years of steady recovery. The upward trend that had returned after the 2023 downturn failed to hold, with shipments slipping again even as some markets continued to show resilience in H1 2026. The change becomes clearer when the recent history is put together. Germany exported 151,000 tonnes in H1 2022, but the volume dropped to 138,000 tonnes in H1 2023, down 8.6 per cent. Exports then began to recover, reaching 141,000 tonnes in H1 2024, up 2.2 per cent, and 144,000 tonnes in H1 2025, an increase of 2.1 per cent, according to ITC data. In H1 2026, however, exports fell back to 140,000 tonnes, down 2.8 per cent year on year. The decline is relatively modest, but it marks a break in the recovery - raising the question of whether Germany's foil exports can regain momentum in the second half of the year. ... Softer demand and rising competition weigh on exports The H1 2026 decline came mainly as demand softened in key European markets while industrial activity remained under pressure. Germany depends heavily on nearby European buyers, and weaker manufacturing, packaging and end-user demand reduced new orders and encouraged more cautious inventory management. Demand for thin-gauge and standard foil also remained subdued, particularly in flexible packaging and household applications. At the same time, German producers faced stronger competition from lower-cost suppliers, making it harder to maintain export volumes in price-sensitive markets. High energy, labour and conversion costs added to the pressure. These costs continued to affect the competitiveness of German foil producers against suppliers from lower-cost regions. Softer demand outside Europe and greater availability from alternative suppliers further limited overseas orders. ... The destination data shows that Germany's export weakness was not spread evenly across its major markets. France remained the leading destination among the five, with German aluminium foil exports increasing from 22,000 tonnes in H1 2025 to 24,000 tonnes in H1 2026, up 9.1 per cent. Shipments stood at 11,000 tonnes in both Q1 and Q2 2025, before rising to 13,000 tonnes in Q1 2026 and easing to 11,000 tonnes in Q2. Switzerland, by comparison, saw exports decline from 24,000 tonnes in H1 2025 to 23,000 tonnes in H1 2026, down 4.2 per cent. Shipments fell from 13,000 tonnes in Q1 2025 to 11,000 tonnes in Q2, remained at 11,000 tonnes in Q1 2026, and then increased to 12,000 tonnes in Q2. The United States received 10,300 tonnes of German aluminium foil in H1 2025, compared with 9,900 tonnes in H1 2026, a decline of 3.9 per cent. Exports rose from 4,600 tonnes in Q1 2025 to 5,700 tonnes in Q2, then dropped to 4,000 tonnes in Q1 2026 before rebounding to 5,900 tonnes in Q2, up 47.5 per cent quarter on quarter. The Netherlands recorded the largest H1 decline among the five destinations. Exports fell from 12,800 tonnes in H1 2025 to 10,600 tonnes in H1 2026, down 17.2 per cent. Shipments stood at 6,400 tonnes in both Q1 and Q2 2025, before falling to 4,900 tonnes in Q1 2026 and recovering to 5,700 tonnes in Q2. ... Germany's aluminium foil exports could remain under pressure in H2 2026 after falling 2.8 per cent year on year to 140,000 tonnes in H1. Exports did improve from 69,000 tonnes in Q1 to 71,000 tonnes in Q2, but Q2 was still below the 72,000 tonnes recorded in Q2 2025. A similar decline was seen in H2 2025, when exports fell from 72,000 tonnes in Q2 to 68,000 tonnes in Q3 and 65,000 tonnes in Q4. If a similar trend continues in 2026, exports could fall to around 67,000 tonnes in Q3 and 64,000 tonnes in Q4. This would put H2 exports at about 131,000 tonnes and full-year 2026 exports at around 271,000 tonnes, pointing to a mild decline rather than a strong recovery.

headline: US tariff cut on Canadian aluminum won't lower Midwest Premium by much: Alcoa | S&P Global
summary_text: Import-reliant US will need broader tariff cuts to lower prices Alcoa seeing strong packaging and rod demand Reducing the US 50% tariff on Canadian primary aluminum will not significantly reduce the US Aluminum Midwest Premium, according to Molly Beerman, CFO of aluminum giant Alcoa. Trade talks between the US and Canada in late August came close to an agreement that would have reduced US 50% tariffs on Canadian aluminum to 25%, but collapsed on Aug. 21. The failed negotiations have led to retaliatory tariffs between the two nations on metals and other goods. The US is heavily reliant on imports of primary aluminum from Canada, but Alcoa does not expect sky-high US aluminum prices to be reduced by much if a preferential rate were given to Canada. "Even if we were to have a favorable rate with Canada, we don't see the Midwest [Premium] dropping significantly," Beerman said Sept. 10 at the Jeffries Global Industrials Conference. "It might come off a little bit, but we wouldn't see it returning to pre-tariff levels." ... Platts assessed the spot 99.7% P1020 US Aluminum Transaction Premium at $1.097/pound plus LME cash, delivered Midwest, net 30-day payment terms, on Sept. 10. Platts is part of S&P Global Energy. The assessment, known as the Midwest Premium, is over four times higher than it was at the start of 2025, primarily due to US 50% tariffs on aluminum and the war in the Middle East. "The US needs to import 4 million metric tons of supply," Beerman said. "Canada only has the possibility to supply about 3 million of that. If additional trade partners get tariff relief or waivers and the last 1 million metric tons is covered, then you can expect the Midwest Premium to reduce in response." headline: The delivery challenge of NBRPs: second part of the study | Eurogypsum
summary_text: The second and final part of the study expands the analysis to 15 draft Natonal Building Renovation Plans. Published on October 22, 2026 With energy prices putting renewed pressure on European households and businesses, accelerating building renovation is more important than ever. It is essential not only to reduce energy bills and to strengthen energy security, but also to make homes healthier and more comfortable. National Building Renovation Plans (NBRPs) offer a key opportunity to align stakeholders, scale up proven solutions and turn Europe’s building energy goals into measurable results. Eurogypsum, together with nine other organisations, is pleased to present the second and final part of “The delivery challenge of NBRPs”, developed by CLIMACT. Building on the first assessment published in May, this release expands the analysis to 15 draft plans: Spain, Netherlands, France, Romania, Slovenia, Poland, Belgium-Wallonia, Finland, Germany, Croatia, Denmark, Austria, Bulgaria, Sweden and Portugal. ###### Ambition is there, but delivery readiness is lagging. ‍ While all 15 plans set long-term decarbonisation objectives, none reaches the delivery-ready threshold. The challenge is no longer setting targets but translating them into actionable renovation pathways. ###### The solutions already exist, but need to be connected and scaled. Across the 15 plans, promising practices in financing, one-stop shops, regulatory frameworks and renovation delivery are emerging. Stronger coordination, peer learning and integrated delivery systems can turn these individual successes into effective national strategies. ###### Major gaps remain in financing, implementation and social safeguards. ‍ Plans often lack secured funding, clear regulatory timelines, adequate delivery capacity and robust monitoring frameworks. Social robustness is the weakest dimension, with insufficient attention to who bears the costs of renovation. With the European Commission and Member States discussing the EPBD implementation today, and the deadline for submitting final NBRPs approaching at the end of 2026, this is a crucial moment to turn ambition into action. headline: M&E sector holds firm
summary_text: The mechanical & electrical (M&E) contracting market has shown impressive resilience in the face of challenging economic conditions, according to a new report from the Building Engineering Services Association (BESA). In the latest edition of its annual survey of the largest firms in the sector, the Association reports a collective turnover recovery from £4.7bn in the wake of the pandemic to over £6bn today. “We have been in a state of flux for some years now,” said Gokhan Hassan managing director of GHCS and GH Engage, which carried out the financial research for the Top 30 UK M&E Contractors report. “Since recovering from Covid in 2022/23 the collective turnover figure has risen from £4.7BN to more than £6bn which coincides with the explosion of the mission critical sector.” The report shows that data centres and the wider digital infrastructure market along with healthcare, defence, energy transition and the push for compliance with building safety legislation are feeding into market growth. However, the fall in residential work has held back parts of the industry and led to the collapse of some highly respected and long-established firms. Office construction and fit-out is providing a steady pipeline of work and new entrants into these markets are evidence of sector resilience. PFI ‘hand backs’ to the NHS estate are also creating a huge refurbishment and retrofit opportunity for the industry, according to BESA’s research. Growth “The future of the M&E sector is bright; the evolution of the Building Safety Act (BSA), intelligent buildings, resilient MEP infrastructure and environmental awareness will propel building services to contribute even further towards economic growth,” added Hassan. Other significant factors emerge from the report such as the importance of investing in innovation and improving the efficiency of processes to keep up with the demands of clients in the digital, defence and healthcare markets. Many firms say they have moved on from the sector’s traditional “first past the post” approach to tenders and are improving efficiency in design and delivery. ... However, several of the firms featured in the report said that protecting margins and cash flow continued to be challenging due to persistent inflation, coupled with fixed-price contracts and project delays, which increased risks and harmed profitability. Critical As a result, M&E contractors are now being more selective about the work they take on by focusing primarily on sectors offering more resilient, longer-term pipelines, such as mission-critical infrastructure and retrofit, and relationships with clients who engage them earlier in the design process. Several also highlighted the importance of proposed legislation to outlaw retentions and crack down on unfair payment practices as critical to protecting cash flow and reducing the risk of insolvency.
