headline: From renovation targets to investment pipelines: financing building renovation at scale | BUILD UP
summary_text: ### The investment challenge behind Europe’s renovation targets Renovating the building stock to high energy efficiency standards is one of the largest investment challenges of the European energy transition. According to the Commission’s 2026 report on energy efficiency financing in Europe, the EU’s total investment needs for energy efficiency are estimated at over €370 billion per year between 2021 and 2030. The largest share of these investment needs relates to building efficiency measures, including heating and cooling refurbishment, amounting to €242 billion per year from 2021 to 2030 to meet the 2030 energy efficiency targets. Most of the investments will focus on residential buildings, contributing to the availability of affordable and quality housing. Against those needs, roughly €200 billion a year was actually invested in energy efficiency across Europe between 2021 and 2023, leaving an annual investment gap of about €170 billion. EU and national public funding together cover only around 15% of estimated investment needs, highlighting the scale of private capital that will need to be mobilised alongside public resources. ... The new Multiannual Financial Framework for 2028–2034, currently under negotiation, maintains several channels that can support building renovation, including national plans, the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), the InvestEU Instrument, and the Social Climate Fund financed from emissions trading revenuesfinanced from emissions trading revenues (mainly the auctioning of allowances under the new ETS2 for buildings and road transport), with Member States contributing at least 25% of the estimated cost of their social climate plans. However, it does not yet guarantee. Recovery and Resilience Facility and Cohesion Policy. The revised EPBD strengthens the framework for financing building renovation, with particular attention to vulnerable households and worst-performing buildings. It also requires Member States to ensure access to one-stop shops, which can help building owners navigate technical, administrative and financing aspects of renovation. At the same time, the scale of the investment challenge means that public funding alone will not be sufficient. Public resources can therefore play an important role in structuring and de-risking investment and in mobilising additional private capital. ... With the first wave of draft National Building Renovation Plans (NBRPs) now submitted, Member States are beginning to translate the revised EPBD into national renovation pathways. According to the Joint Research Centre’s assessment, reported annual energy renovation rates range from 0.7% to 5.7%, with most falling between 1% and 3%. These figures represent planned trajectories rather than achieved renovation rates: the EU’s deep renovation rate has remained at around 0.2% per year, compared with the approximately 2% considered necessary to meet the 2030 objectives. The draft plans also reveal substantial differences in estimated investment needs across Member States. Public funding generally accounts for between 20% and 30% of renovation costs, while only seven draft plans explicitly address the mobilisation of private finance. Turning these plans into credible investment pathways will therefore be an important part of scaling up renovation. ... Despite the strengthened regulatory and financial framework, building renovation remains difficult to finance at scale. Many of the technical solutions are already available, but investment pipelines and local delivery capacity remain insufficient to support deployment at the pace required. Policy and regulatory, financial, technical, and social barriers are well documented and largely shared across Europe. Overcoming these hurdles requires an investment-ready ecosystem that no longer leans on public subsidy alone, but integrates all necessary elements: stable policy signals; one-stop shops that cut transaction costs by combining technical advice, financial guidance and contractor coordination; NBRPs that work as investment roadmaps rather than target lists; aggregation and project-development assistance that bundle small projects through municipalities, housing associations, ESCOs and district-scale renovation into the pipeline scale investors need; and grants reserved for vulnerable households and worst-performing buildings. ... Moving beyond financial instruments, industrialised, off-site renovation methods, including prefabricated façades and standardised heat pump packages, can reduce construction time and cost uncertainty, helping to make project performance more predictable and improve bankability. This approach is explored further in BUILD UP’s technical article on the DIGIFAB project. ... | Barrier addressed | Type of good practice | Instrument (how it unlocks investment) | Projects/ example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Complex user journey | One-stop shops, integrated building renovation services, municipal advisory hubs | One-stop shops, EPBD Article 18 (aggregate demand and bundle small projects into investable portfolios, cutting the cost and time of arranging a renovation). | Turnkey Retrofit / Solutions4Renovation (FR, IE, ES); PadovaFIT Expanded (IT); re-MODULEES; ComActivate Resource Centres; CoachCopro condominium service (Paris) | | Lack of finance | Soft loans, grants, guarantees, green mortgages, revolving funds, EIB/national promotional bank schemes | Grants and capital subsidies (buy down capital expenditure; can be reserved for vulnerable households, as the EPBD requires); blended finance, grant or subsidy + loan (public money takes the first-loss slice, stretching private capital several times further); guarantees, InvestEU and Cohesion financial instruments (cover losses so lenders offer longer, cheaper loans without spending the principal). | KfW programmes (DE); KredEx Revolving Fund (EE); WSW guarantee fund (NL); Energy Efficient Mortgages Initiative (EeMAP); European Investment Bank (EIB) European Local Energy Assistance (ELENA) project-development assistance | | Small project size | Aggregation through municipalities, housing associations, apartment blocks, ESCOs and district renovation | Aggregation and project-development assistance (build the pipeline scale investors need); Energy Performance Contracting (an ESCO guarantees the savings and is paid from them, keeping the works off constrained public balance sheets). | SUPERSHINE district renovation (IT, DK, LV); RenoWatt public-building pooling (BE); Energiesprong aggregated social-housing procurement (NL); ComActivate homeowner-association aggregation | | Lack of trust | Quality assurance, certified installers, standard contracts, post-renovation checks | Energy Performance ... - Romania. An uncapped InvestEU guarantee that moves risk off bank balance sheets. Romania channelled national EU funds into the InvestEU Member State compartment, where the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) uses them to issue €220.6 million of uncapped, unfunded portfolio guarantees to commercial lenders. The guarantee absorbs credit risk on newly generated portfolios of energy-efficiency, renewable-energy and sustainable-transport loans, so banks can lend to borrowers from households to large corporates on better terms and with lower collateral requirements; the EBRD expects the framework to mobilise more than €270 million of new green financing, with Libra Internet Bank the first institution onboarded and further banks expected to join. It is paired with technical assistance funded through the InvestEU Advisory Hub, without which most local banks would lack the capacity to originate eligible loans. The case illustrates how guarantees can encourage lending without requiring public authorities to provide the underlying capital, particularly where perceived risk rather than a lack of available capital is constraining investment. - Wallonia (Belgium). RenoWatt: aggregation that makes public buildings investable. RenoWatt, supported by the EIB’s ELENA facility, acts as a one-stop shop for Belgian public authorities: it audits buildings, selects those worth renovating, pools them across municipalities into single tenders and structures the contracts – usually energy performance contracts in which an ESCO guarantees the savings and is paid from them. Close to a hundred municipalities, provinces, hospitals and emergency services have joined; signed projects represent more than €100 million in investment, and individual buildings are achieving 30–40% primary energy reductions. Aggregation is central to the model: pooling buildings across participating public authorities can create portfolios large enough to attract ESCOs and lenders and enable projects to be procured at scale. The model is particularly relevant to EPBD Article 18, as it illustrates how a one-stop shop can support project development and procurement in addition to providing advice. - France. CoachCopro: a one-stop shop that scaled from a city to a country. Condominiums are among the hardest segments to renovate, because any decision needs a majority of owners with different finances and time horizons. CoachCopro, created by the Paris Climate Agency with the City of Paris and the French Agency for Ecological Transition (ADEME), gives condominium boards a single route through the process: a step-by-step method, cost benchmarks, a register of qualified professionals and a durable record of the building’s renovation history. More than a third of Paris condominiums are registered on it, and its operating costs are relatively limited compared with the investment required for renovation itself – roughly €200,000 to build and €80,000 a year to run. Its subsequent integration into the national France Rénov’ service illustrates how an established one-stop-shop model can be adapted and scaled beyond its original local context. - Greece. Exoikonomo: ranking applications by the cost of the energy they save. Greece has implemented the EXOIKONOMO residential renovation programme through eight rounds over 13 years, moving from National Strategic Reference Framework (NSRF) and European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) resources to the Recovery and Resilience Facility and supporting more than 200,000 energy interventions. The programme combines subsidies of between 50% and 100%, depending on income and social criteria, with interest-free loans provided through four banks. Eligible projects must achieve an improvement of at least three EPC energy classes, reach a minimum EPC class B, and deliver primary energy savings of more than 30%.

It provides a working template for lowering carbon footprints while still delivering premium, fully let space in a prime location.

headline: S&P Global Eurozone Construction PMI®: Steeper Fall In New Orders Drives Sharper Decline - ConstructUK
summary_text: # S&P Global Eurozone Construction PMI®: Steeper Fall in New Orders Drives Sharper Decline 4th September 2026 Key findings: - New orders contract at fastest pace since April - Employment falls again as outlook remains pessimistic - Cost pressures continue to soften Construction firms in the eurozone saw the pace of decline in total activity accelerate in August amid a sharper contraction in new business. New order intakes decreased at the quickest rate in four months, while all three monitored sub-sectors saw sustained falls in activity midway through the third quarter. At the same time, there were sharp reductions in both employment and purchasing, and cost inflation remained historically marked despite easing to a six-month low. The S&P Global Eurozone Construction PMI Total Activity Index — a seasonally adjusted index tracking monthly changes in total industry activity — posted 43.0 in August, down from 44.3 in July to signal a stronger contraction in construction activity midway through the third quarter. Total activity has now decreased consistently for 52 months. The steeper fall in construction activity reflected an accelerated decline in France that was the most pronounced since May 2020, while Italian firms saw the fastest contraction for four years. German companies meanwhile bucked the downward index level trend to register its softest reduction in 2026 to date. By sector, housing activity decreased at the sharpest rate , followed closely by commercial construction. Civil engineering activity saw the softest decrease of the three, but one that was still solid overall. In line with the picture for total construction activity, the rate of decline in new orders gathered pace during August. New business was down markedly and at the strongest rate since April. New orders fell notably sharply in France, while there was a renewed and solid drop in Italy. Construction orders in Germany declined at a softer rate than that seen in July, but at one that was still substantial. Employment moderated for the seventh month in a row in August, with the rate of job shedding the most prominent in four months. Steeper reduction in workforce numbers were recorded in France and Germany, while staffing levels in Italy rose for the second successive month. Eurozone constructors decreased their usage of subcontractors again, and at a marked rate. As a result, the availability of subcontractors rose, though the rate of increase was only modest. ... Higher cost burdens continued to weigh on the construction sector. The rate of input cost inflation eased further from April’s peak to reach a six-month low, but remained well above the series average. The rise in input costs in Italy slowed on the month, contrasting with a slight acceleration in input cost inflation in both Germany and France. In line with this trend, the rise in subcontractor rates was the softest since February. At the same time, construction firms also scaled back their purchasing activity during August. Input buying has fallen continuously on a monthly basis since June 2022. The latest reduction was unchanged from July. French and German firms saw softer decreases in input buying, contrasting with the sharpest fall in purchasing activity since January 2023 in Italy. While demand for inputs fell, constructions firms continued to face a further lengthening of suppliers’ delivery times, the thirteenth in as many months. Lead times lengthened solidly, though the latest deterioration was the softest since February. ... Eurozone construction companies gave a downbeat assessment regarding the prospects for activity growth over the coming year. The degree of pessimism was unchanged from July’s three-month record. French companies posted the most pessimistic outlook, posting the weakest level of sentiment since April. German firms also posted a markedly downbeat outlook. Firms in Italy meanwhile registered the most positive outlook for six months.

headline: The application of the European Union's new Construction Products Regulation is progressing. But slowly. – Construction Industry RT
summary_text: RTT The new European Union Construction Products Regulation (2024/3110), which replaces the old regulation (2011/305), entered into force in its entirety in January 2026. However, this does not mean that the new regulation should be complied with in any respect, or even that it could be complied with immediately after entry into force. The new Construction Products Regulation will be implemented over a long transition period, product group by product group, through standardization and European Technical Assessment Documents. The overall transition from the current system under the old regulation to the CE marking system under the new regulation must be completed by 1 January 2040. In order for the new Construction Products Regulation to be applicable to the CE marking of construction products, all of the approximately 450 currently valid harmonised product standards must be replaced by new product standards with their reference standards. This will also likely increase the number of standards somewhat. This enormous work requires, as a first step, that the European Commission prepare new product group-specific standardisation requests to be submitted to the standardisation organisation CEN. This will take place in the Commission's ongoing CPR acquis process. After this, new standards must be drawn up for each product group, a task that typically takes at least three years for each individual standard. The aforementioned Commission acquis process has been proactively underway for several years and there are currently well over a dozen groups preparing standardisation requests. However, only one standardisation request under the new regulation has been completed by 2025, concerning cements. The next standardisation request for doors and windows is expected to be completed this year. However, the Commission's acquis list already includes 36 different product groups for which standardisation requests should be prepared, so the implementation of the new regulation has not progressed at all at the planned pace so far.

headline: Building renovation is the new driving force behind construction. Europe is preparing investments for decades to come.
summary_text: Aug 18, 2026 Europe is preparing for one of the largest waves of building renovations in its history. National renovation plans resulting from the revised EPBD are expected to determine the scale of investment by 2030, 2040, and 2050. This represents a significant shift for the construction industry: an increasing portion of demand for materials may come not from new investments but from thermal modernization and adapting existing buildings to new energy standards. In July, the European Commission published the first assessment of 16 draft National Building Renovation Plans (NBPs), prepared in connection with the revised EPBD. The documents are intended to provide countries with concrete building renovation paths by 2030, 2040, and 2050, identifying investment needs, financing sources, and actions that will lead to a highly energy-efficient and decarbonized building stock. The Commission notes that the plans can create a predictable portfolio of renovation projects for the coming years. From the construction industry's perspective, this is a more important signal than another climate change declaration. Europe is beginning to translate its energy transformation into a multi-year investment program. Existing buildings account for over 30% of the EU's energy consumption, so improving their efficiency will require not individual renovations but a massive modernization of the entire building stock. This, in turn, could mean a fundamental shift for building materials producers. For years, we have assessed the sector's condition primarily through the lens of new investments. Meanwhile, an increasing portion of future demand will stem from the need to modernize buildings, improve their energy efficiency, and adapt them to new standards. ... This is clearly visible in the French, Portuguese, and Romanian markets, where Selena Group has been consistently building its presence for years. The European Commission has already scrutinized the draft national building renovation plans of these countries. France aims to reduce final energy consumption in buildings by 36% by 2050, with nearly 2 billion square meters of residential space to be modernized. In the long term, this will drive growing demand in the French market not only for technologies that improve building energy performance, but also for efficient local channels for their delivery. It's no coincidence that Selena recently strengthened its position in this market by acquiring ACDIS France, a well-established distributor of building materials trusted by local construction subcontractors. The scale of this trend is even more pronounced in Portugal, where, according to a project reviewed by the European Commission, over half a million square meters of residential space is to be renovated by 2050 – as much as 84% ​​of the stock covered by the 2020 database. This is no longer a single modernization program, but a reconstruction of a vast portion of the market. It is crucial for Selena that we consistently develop our expertise in waterproofing and thermal modernization in Portugal – first through the acquisition of Imperalum, a Portuguese manufacturer of bituminous felt, in 2023, and last year a 66% stake in Grupo IGM, a manufacturer of sandwich panels. This is an example of how a long-term acquisition strategy can respond to a structural shift in demand before its full scale becomes apparent in market data. ... Interesting conclusions were also drawn from the assessment of the Romanian market, which was Selena's first foreign expansion destination. The country plans to reduce energy consumption in buildings by 53% by 2050, and modernize 70% of residential buildings and 80% of non-residential buildings. This demonstrates that the enormous renovation potential lies not only in the most developed markets of Western Europe. Central and Eastern Europe will also be one of the largest construction sites in the coming decades.

headline: Construction Products Regulation (CPR): Kiwa and Vinçotte in the final stages of becoming a Notified Body
summary_text: The Construction Products Regulation (CPR) reshapes how manufacturers demonstrate product performance, sustainability and compliance. Environmental transparency is a mandatory part of the process, with implications for declarations, data collection, market access and CE marking. Kiwa GmbH is in the final stages of extending its activities to become a Notified Body for the CPR. Vinçotte, a Kiwa company, with a strong position in the Belgian market as an EPD verifier, will build on Kiwa GmbH’s Notified Body status to continue supporting clients in the construction products sector. The same applies for other countries where Kiwa already has Notified Bodies for the technical requirements of the CPR like Italy, the Baltic States or Türkiye. ... ## What is changing under the CPR? The CPR, adopted in 2024, strengthens the EU’s approach to environmental sustainability for construction products. Manufacturers must now include environmental sustainability information as part of the combined Declaration of Performance and Conformity (DoPC). Previously, the Declaration of Performance (DoP) focused primarily on product performance and safety. Under the updated CPR, this evolves into the DoPC, which also includes environmental sustainability data based on life-cycle impacts. ## The projected timing The introduction of mandatory environmental reporting will take place in phases. The projected timing is: ### 2026 Mandatory reporting of Global Warming Potential (GWP). ### 2030 Mandatory reporting of core environmental impact indicators. ### 2032 Mandatory reporting of additional environmental impact indicators. The timing also depends on the availability of harmonised standards for individual product categories. The European Commission has published projected timings for the development of these standards. ... ## Kiwa and Vinçotte as Notified Body for the CPR The updated Assessment and Verification System (AVS) introduces a new System 3+. This makes verification of reported environmental impacts mandatory and requires: - Initial inspection of manufacturing plants - Validation and verification of company-specific environmental data Kiwa GmbH is part of the Kiwa group of more than 20 Notified Bodies and is already active as an EPD verification body. It is now in the final stages of extending these activities to become a Notified Body for the CPR. For manufacturers, working with a Notified Body such as Kiwa GmbH provides independent verification to support CE marking under the updated CPR. Vinçotte, a Kiwa company, has a strong position in the Belgian market as an EPD verifier. By leveraging the Notified Body status of Kiwa GmbH, Vinçotte’s verifiers will be qualified under Kiwa’s accreditation. This will enable Vinçotte to continue serving its clients in the construction products sector. The same applies for other countries where Kiwa already has Notified Bodies for the technical requirements of the CPR like Italy, the Baltic States or Türkiye. ... ## Digital Product Passport The revised CPR also introduces, for the first time, a mandatory Digital Product Passport (DPP) for construction products placed on the EU market. The exact requirements will become enforceable once the supporting harmonised standards and delegated acts have been adopted. The Digital Product Passport will include information such as: - Product identification - Materials and components - Environmental impacts - Product performance - Safety information - Life-cycle information Kiwa is following the ongoing standardization work and plans to offer its clients a Digital Product Passport solution that conforms to the upcoming standards.

headline: Energy Efficiency: EBC signs joint statement calling for effective implementation of the EPBD and predictability - EBC ConstructionEBC Construction
summary_text: The European Builders Confederation, together with 26 other building and energy sector organisations, signed a joint statement calling on the European Commission and Member States to ensure the revised Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD) is not only transposed on paper, but properly implemented and enforced in practice. The statement follows the Commission’s decision, on 15 July, to open infringement procedures against all 27 Member States for failing to fully transpose the recast EPBD (Directive (EU) 2024/1275) by the 29 May 2026 deadline. Progress across Member States remains mixed: some are developing practical tools, but many remain delayed or have transposed the text without the guidance needed to apply it. I n the joint statement, the signatories stress that a proper EPBD implementation matters for market certainty. Companies and public authorities need to know the rules agreed at EU level will actually be applied, with many having already invested on that basis. Delays risk undermining that confidence, a concern that weighs particularly heavily on construction SMEs and craft trades, which have the least room to absorb regulatory uncertainty. The statement calls on the Commission and national authorities to fully transpose the EPBD without weakening existing provisions, provide clear guidance on how compliance can be demonstrated, run information campaigns for citizens and building owners, develop proportionate verification and inspection routes, use standardisation to avoid too fragmented national approaches, and invest in the skills and administrative capacity needed to apply the rules consistently on the ground. The signatories also underline the role of regions, cities and energy agencies in delivering the EPBD, calling for their involvement in transposition and for social safeguards and stable financing so implementation reaches those who need it most. The renovation market represents the main field of activity for the majority of the 94% micro companies in the construction sector. The joint statement builds on EBC’s ongoing engagement on the EPBD, as, and on its continued dialogue with national members on real-time transposition and implementation.

headline: SW Machines: FMS Key to India Manufacturing Shift
summary_text: SW Machines has built its reputation around high-productivity machining solutions. How is the company’s portfolio of machining systems, automation modules and complete manufacturing cells evolving to meet the changing requirements of Indian manufacturers seeking greater productivity, flexibility and shorter production cycles? At SW Machines, we focus on maximum productivity per square metre. Indian manufacturers need shorter cycles, better quality, and flexibility to meet changing demand. We are therefore moving beyond standalone machining centres with multi-spindle systems, automation modules, pallet handling, and manufacturing cells that increase output and reduce cost. SW’s modular approach lets customers start with one machining centre and scale toward full automation. As EV, aerospace, medical, and precision engineering grow, our flexible systems help customers manage variants, shorten cycles, and stay future-ready. ... Automation is increasingly moving from individual machines to integrated manufacturing systems. What role do SW’s automation modules, robotic cells and turnkey solutions play in helping customers move towards lights-out or highly autonomous production? Automation is now about integrated production systems that operate with minimal human intervention while maintaining consistent quality. SW offers robotic handling, pallet automation, tool management, part tracking, process monitoring, and turnkey cells to improve utilisation, reduce labour dependency, and deliver predictable output. Many customers aim for lights-out production. SW supports this through intelligent automation and process integration, especially in automotive, EV, and high-volume precision machining, where higher utilisation directly improves profitability. ... Flexible Manufacturing Systems will be key to India’s manufacturing transformation over the next decade. While Indian manufacturers traditionally used dedicated lines for high-volume production, today’s market demands customisation, shorter runs, and faster model changes. FMS enables multiple components to be produced on one system with high utilisation and consistent quality. The strongest potential is in automotive, EV, aerospace, commercial vehicles, industrial machinery, watch industry, hydraulic industry, and precision engineering, especially among Tier-1 suppliers managing multiple variants to global quality standards. headline: Ethereal Machines CNC and Machining-as-a-Service explained
summary_text: BENGALURU: Most Indian machine shops buy their CNC machines from Germany, Japan, Taiwan or China, and the controllers that run them almost always come from abroad. Ethereal Machines, a Bengaluru company started in 2014, took the harder route. It designs and builds its own 3-axis and 5-axis CNC machines, runs them on its own factory floor, and sells the finished parts to aerospace, medical and electronics customers. That model, which the company calls Machining-as-a-Service, has drawn real money. In June 2026 Ethereal announced a US$28.5 million Series B round led by Avataar Ventures, with existing investor Peak XV Partners also taking part. Here is what the company does and what it plans to do with that cheque. ... A CNC machine cuts metal or plastic by following a computer program. A basic 3-axis machine moves its cutting tool left and right, forward and back, and up and down. A 5-axis machine can also tilt and rotate the part or the tool, so it can reach awkward angles in a single setup. That matters for parts like turbine blades, aerospace brackets and medical implants, where curved surfaces and tight tolerances leave little room for error. Ethereal makes two machine lines, according to its website. Nimbus is its 5-axis platform and Aura is a 3-axis machine built for production work. Both are designed, assembled and tested in-house. The company says tolerances on its parts go as low as plus or minus 0.005 mm, which it validates for each part family, and that every part is probed on the machine and checked on a coordinate measuring machine before it ships. ... The interesting choice is the business model. Ethereal does not mainly sell its machines to other factories. A customer uploads a 3D model or drawing, the company's engineers review whether the part can be made and flag risks, and they send back a quote and lead time. The site says it never issues automatic quotes. Parts are then cut, inspected and shipped from Bengaluru with material certificates and inspection reports. It holds AS9100D certification, the quality standard used across the aerospace supply chain, along with ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 for information security. It also follows AS9102B for first-article inspection. Those badges are what let a small supplier bid for work on aircraft and space programmes, where buyers insist on full traceability for each part. ... The company's announcement lists five uses for the money. The biggest is a new 300,000 sq ft factory on the outskirts of Bengaluru, under a memorandum of understanding with the Government of Karnataka. The second is what Ethereal describes as India's first indigenous multi-axis CNC controller, the electronics and software brain of a machine that the company says has until now been imported. The rest of the list covers an AI-driven factory software platform meant to turn a drawing into a validated production process, new teams in the United States and Europe to serve overseas customers directly, and more capacity for precision parts in aerospace, healthcare, semiconductors and consumer electronics.

headline: Interview – Jean Pascal Bobst and Ashish Saxena at Bobst India's 30th Anniversary Celebrations - Packaging South Asia
summary_text: While many of our meetings have come with a geopolitical crisis in the background, our conversations have always discussed the company’s ambition to do more in India, transfer more technology to Pune, and strengthen its resources and structure. More than fifteen years ago at the Bobst factory in Pune, with the global financial crisis in the background, Bobst explained his readiness to do whatever necessary to maintain the liquidity of the company and continue its investments in Brazil, China and India. When we interviewed the Bobst Group Ceo at drupa24, the Ukraine war had increased energy and steel prices in Europe, putting the company’s operations, customers, and employees under pressure. Nevertheless, he revealed bold and specific plans for manufacturing expansion at the Pune location, including building a second factory on nearby land for manufacturing components, FFG corrugated machines, vacuum metallizers, and other projects. ... By the time of our recent meeting in Pune, much of what Bobst had said in Dusseldorf had already come to fruition. The 30th anniversary celebration of the company in India was accompanied by the inauguration of the Bobst Competence Center in Pune and a grand Open House. Vacuum metallizers are in serial production and being exported – the seventh machine is on the shop floor of the new factory. The NovaFFG machines have also been rolling out – quick job changeovers were demonstrated live at the competence center. (The Open House also included demonstrations of the Novacut 106 enhanced with Accuregister and Zero patching, the Novafold enhanced with Accubraille, Vision CI flexo press and the Novalam 800 laminator.) ... Essentially affirming his comments to us at drupa 24, Jean Pascal Bobst said that several of the ambitious plans he revealed two years ago for the Pune factories have already been implemented, and others continue to progress. “The geopolitical constraints of the last several years, including Covid, Ukraine and tariffs, have disrupted or affected various global supply chains and financial structures. With steep changes in currency exchange rates and higher interest costs, the European-manufactured Bobst machines have become, in some cases, unaffordable for Indian customers. Bobst will run fast, adjust, and even revise its strategy to cope with changes. “We will continue to move to regions and to countries. With China for China, India for India strategies, we will enhance capabilities in each. And if we are not able to offer everything, we will partner with others. Two years ago, we said that to de-risk China, we would double our capacity in India, and we expect 20% of the increased production will be absorbed in India while 80% will go to exports. Ashish Saxena, managing director of Bobst’s India operations, said the company’s immediate strategy had three main priorities: accelerating domestic growth, establishing India as a global manufacturing and services hub, and strengthening the foundational capabilities required to support that expansion. On expansion across South Asia, Saxena said these markets were smaller than India but had broadly similar requirements and were already buying Bobst equipment. The company plans to increase its sales coverage in the region and strengthen its agent network where direct coverage is not possible. “Our first and foremost aim is to customize and adapt our global portfolios and technologies and potentially do something that is purely India for India,” he said, adding, “India’s diverse customer base requires equipment and solutions to be adapted to different converter segments.” The second priority is to expand India’s role within Bobst’s global manufacturing network, including through increased production, R&D, engineering services and software development. The third is to strengthen capabilities in areas including engineering, innovation, services and the sales network. “We want to be able to sell solutions to our customers and not just offer a machine,” he said.

The dependence is even higher in sophisticated applications such as aerospace and defence. That import gap is now becoming an investment opportunity. As India pushes for greater manufacturing self-reliance, the focus is shifting from simply assembling finished products locally to building more of the machinery and critical components that make them. Two listed companies offer a direct play on this trend: Jyoti CNC Automation and Macpower CNC Machines. Both are benefiting from the same import-substitution and indigenisation story. ... ## Jyoti CNC Automation: The Scale Play Jyoti CNC Automation is India’s largest listed pure-play CNC machine-tool maker. But its advantage is not just scale. The company has built a deeply backward-integrated manufacturing hub in Rajkot, producing critical components such as spindles, automatic tool changers, and rotary tables in-house. This integration matters because these are high-value assemblies that many domestic manufacturers still import. Producing them in-house lowers machine costs while supporting gross margins, which stood at 58% in Q1 FY27. The company also has access to advanced European technology through its French subsidiary, Huron Graffenstaden. Its 5-axis machining capabilities are particularly relevant for aerospace and defence, where India remains heavily dependent on imported high-precision machines. ... . However, what’s important is the order book. At the end of June 2026, the order book stood at ₹4,848 crore, equivalent to almost 2.5 times FY26 revenue. Aerospace and defence accounted for 38% of the book, followed by general engineering at 20% and auto and auto components at 19%. ... ## Scaling Up Capacity Capacity is the next leg of the story. Jyoti operated at around 90% utilisation in FY26, leaving limited room for volume growth. It is now investing ₹450 crore to increase annual capacity from 6,000 to 16,000 machines by September 2026. The company is also moving deeper into import substitution. Its newly launched NX 6240 EY double-column machine, with an estimated ₹3-5 crore average selling price, targets applications in railways, power and heavy engineering. ... ## Risks to Watch Huron is the biggest near-term overhang. French authorities opened a judicial investigation into the subsidiary over alleged violations of EU export controls involving dual-use machine tools exported to Russia via India. The investigation has also affected shipments, leading to around ₹35 crore of revenue being deferred in Q1FY27 as Huron shifted to delivery-based revenue recognition. Management expects these dispatches to be recognised in the second half. Any prolonged regulatory action could further disrupt Huron’s exports and technology access. ... ## Macpower CNC Machines: The Smaller Growth Bet While Jyoti CNC represents the scale and technology-heavy play, Macpower CNC Machines offers exposure to the same manufacturing cycle from a much smaller base. That gives Macpower more room to grow market share and compound revenue at a faster rate, although its smaller scale also makes quarterly execution more sensitive. This debt-free company has developed more than 315 machine models and serves customers across defense, aerospace, auto, electronic manufacturing services, and general engineering. The company is scaling and setting up new plants. About 50% of the new plant’s capacity is planned for defence work and higher-margin products.

summary_text: ## Jyoti CNC Automation approved a ₹1,020.65 crore capital investment over five years for its Rajkot facility under the ECMS scheme. Jyoti CNC Automation has received approval for a capital investment proposal worth ₹1,020.65 crore over the next five years at its existing manufacturing facility in Rajkot, the company said in a stock exchange filing on Monday. The investment proposal has been approved under the Electronic Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Jyoti CNC said it would be eligible for a capital expenditure incentive of up to 25% on the proposed investments under the scheme, subject to the stipulations of the ECMS and the approval letter issued by MeitY on August 17. ... At the operating level, EBITDA increased 8.6% year-on-year to ₹108.8 crore, compared with ₹100.2 crore in the year-ago quarter. The EBITDA margin, however, contracted sharply to 21.4% from 24.4%.

headline: Nine Days Out, HIMTEX 2026 Exhibitor List Locks In at 350-Plus
summary_text: VMPL Hyderabad (Telangana) [India], August 11: Stall allotments for the 9th edition of the Hyderabad International Machine Tool & Engineering Expo (HIMTEX 2026) are now settled, with organisers confirming 350+ exhibitors and 1,000+ live machines for the show, which runs 20-24 August at the HITEX Exhibition Centre, Hyderabad. At 18,500 sqm, this is the largest edition HIMTEX has staged so far. What stands out this year is where the exhibitors are coming from. Companies are travelling in from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Punjab, a spread that organisers say shows how far HIMTEX has grown beyond a Hyderabad-only event. Mr. Vinoth Sasidharan, Project Head, HIMTEX, put it simply: "The evolution of HIMTEX--from a regional exhibition to an event that industry stakeholders deliberately plan to attend--is a clear indicator that we are building something with real industry value." The exhibitor mix is broad this year. CNC machining centres, VMCs, HMCs, sheet metal and forming presses, cutting tools, welding equipment, robotics, and material handling all feature, alongside a growing number of companies working in industrial software and connected manufacturing. That last group ties into one of the biggest draws on this year's show floor: DiFact - the Digital Factory & Connected Technologies Pavilion. Built around the Digital Factory Experience Zone (DFEZ), developed with Knowledge Partner Automation Industry Association (AIA), the pavilion will run live demonstrations of turning and milling operations, CMM inspection, AMR-based material movement, cobot-assisted handling, and machine monitoring dashboards through the week. It is built to be walked through and seen working, rather than just read about on a brochure. "MSMEs hear the words 'Industry 4.0' all the time, but seeing it actually running on a shop floor is still rare for most of them," said Mr. Kuna Shankar, Director, HITEX. "That is exactly what DFEZ is built to show. We would rather let people see it running." Several exhibitors who confirmed their participation this week said scale was the main reason. A single large show tends to bring stronger footfall than several smaller regional ones, and HIMTEX's growing reach across states came up often as the reason for signing up. HIMTEX 2026 continues to be backed by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) and the Machine Tool Manufacturers' Association, Rajkot, along with its Diamond, Gold and Silver partners. Business visitor registration is open now at www.himtex.in. Entry is free for registered visitors aged 18 and above. The Hyderabad International Machine Tool & Engineering Expo (HIMTEX) is the flagship biennial exhibition dedicated to machine tools, manufacturing technologies, industrial automation, and engineering solutions. Bringing together leading manufacturers, technology providers, buyers, and industry professionals, HIMTEX serves as a catalyst for innovation, collaboration, and business growth while supporting the advancement of India's manufacturing sector. Strategic localization of high-precision heavy machinery and proprietary controller tech commercialization will drive mid-term structural margins. ... Standalone performance remains exceptionally strong, while its French subsidiary Huron Graffenstaden is projected to deliver ₹300 cr to ₹325 cr in revenue with positive PAT. ... ## Data Snapshot - The company maintains full-year FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance of 25% to 30% with ~25% EBITDA margins. - Huron Graffenstaden's FY27 revenue is targeted at ₹300 cr to ₹325 cr with standalone EBITDA margins of 8% to 10% and positive PAT. - Capital expenditure for FY27 is projected at ₹200 cr to ₹250 cr, primarily funding a new 10,000-machine annual capacity facility. - Total machine sales for FY27 are anticipated to surpass 8,000 units compared to approximately 5,550 units in FY26. ... ## What's Changed - Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 28.4% in Q1 FY27, up 190 bps YoY, demonstrating excellent domestic pricing power. - The newly developed double-column VMC 'NX' series targets heavy engineering and railway bogies to displace high-value imports. - Developing proprietary CNC controllers, motors, and drives, aiming for technological self-reliance and commercialization within two years. ... - Full-year growth targets of 25% to 30% top-line expansion remain intact despite temporary export licensing hurdles at Huron. - The impending commissioning of the 10,000-unit facility by the end of September 2026 will ease historical capacity constraints. - The yearly order intake guidance is established at ₹2,500 cr to ₹3,000 cr, aligning with massive structural demand in railways, heavy engineering, and power. - Targeted operating cash flow conversion of approximately 50% of EBITDA will support debt discipline, keeping net debt stable at ~₹700 cr. ... While short-term French regulatory headwinds at Huron Graffenstaden created quarterly consolidated margin volatility, Jyoti CNC's standalone strength (~37% YoY domestic surge) illustrates the secular strength of India's manufacturing capex cycle. Sustained value creation will depend on the smooth scale-up of the domestic 10,000-unit facility. ... ## Industry Context The high-precision double-column vertical machining center segment in India has historically relied heavily on foreign OEMs. India imported more than 300 machines in this category last year, with average unit values ranging from ₹3 cr to ₹5 cr. The domestic commercialization of the NX double-column series positions Jyoti CNC at the forefront of the nation's import-substitution push across railways, commercial vehicles, and heavy infrastructure.

headline: Jyoti CNC Automation Q1FY27 standalone revenue up 37% to ₹509 crore
summary_text: Key Highlights Jyoti CNC Automation released the Q1FY27 earnings call transcript, detailing a 37% rise in standalone revenue to ₹509 crore and a 24% increase in consolidated revenue to ₹508.5 crore. The consolidated result was impacted by a change in accounting policy at the Huron subsidiary, which delayed revenue recognition. Management maintained full-year growth guidance of 25-30% and confirmed the new manufacturing facility will begin operations in September 2026. ... ## Operational Updates Management highlighted strong demand across general engineering, automotive, EMS, and defense sectors. The company launched a new high-precision double column machine, NX, targeting the railway and heavy engineering sectors. Capacity utilization stood at 86% in Q1FY27 against a current capacity of 6,000 machines annually. A new facility adding capacity for 10,000 machines is scheduled to commence operations by end-September 2026. The order book stands at ₹4,848 crore. Industry-wise composition includes 38% from aerospace and defense, 20% from general engineering, 19% from automotive, and 13% from EMS. Machine sales reached 1,406 units in Q1FY27, compared to 1,117 units in Q1FY26. ... A key focus of the call was the change in accounting policy at the Huron subsidiary. The company moved away from the percentage-of-completion method due to uncertainties in obtaining end-user certificates for exports outside the European Union, driven by geopolitical tensions. This resulted in lower revenue recognition in Q1FY27. Management stated that like-to-like consolidated revenue would have been higher by more than ₹30 crore had the previous method been applied. Full-year FY27 revenue guidance for Huron is ₹300-325 crore with an EBITDA margin of 8-10%. ... Jyoti CNC has guided for revenue growth of 25% to 30% in FY27, with EBITDA margins targeted around 25% and operating cash flow estimated at 50% of EBITDA. Subsidiary Huron projects FY27 revenue between INR300 crore and INR325 crore, with EBITDA margins of 8% to 10% and positive PAT. The company launched the high-precision NX double-column machine targeting import-substitution sectors and is developing 8-meter and 10-meter machine models alongside proprietary drives, motors, and CNC controllers. Capital expenditure for FY27 is guided at INR200 crore to INR250 crore, with a new 10,000-machine capacity facility set to begin operations by end of September and total machine sales expected to surpass 8,000 units. ... ## New Product Launches and Technology Development Jyoti CNC introduced a new high-precision double-column machine, the NX, targeting sectors that have historically relied on imports. The NX is aimed at the following industries: - Railway sector - Commercial vehicles - Infrastructure - Power - Heavy engineering In addition to the NX, the company is actively developing larger machine models, with 8-meter and 10-meter variants in the pipeline following the launch of the 6-meter model. Jyoti CNC is also developing its own drives, motors, and CNC controllers in-house, with the Human-Machine Interface already ready. The company plans to commercialize these proprietary technologies within two years.

summary_text: Key Highlights Macpower CNC Machines achieved its best-ever quarterly results in Q1FY27 with revenue of ₹95.24 crore and net profit of ₹9.58 crore, driven by a 56% revenue surge and margin expansion to 16.2%. With a ₹456 crore order book and rising average realizations, management increased FY27 growth guidance to over 30% and initiated a ₹50 crore capacity expansion project. macpower cnc machines delivered its highest-ever quarterly performance in Q1FY27, reporting revenue of ₹95.24 crore and net profit (PAT) of ₹9.58 crore, driven by robust order inflows and margin expansion. Following the strong start, Chairman & Managing Director Rupesh Mehta raised the company’s full-year revenue growth guidance to over 30%, up from the previously stated 28–30% range, citing improved visibility on raw materials, manpower, and a growing order book. The company also unveiled plans for a ₹50 crore infrastructure expansion to support future scaling. ... ## Order Book and Pipeline The company’s pending order book stands at ₹456 crore, reflecting a 32% year-on-year increase. Approximately 40% of this order book is attributed to the high-end NEXA series. Management highlighted a robust domestic bid pipeline, with ₹739 crore in submitted bids, ₹304 crore under evaluation, and over ₹1,043 crore in quotations. Rupesh Mehta noted that new order inflow in the quarter was approximately ₹145 crore, against execution of ₹93–94 crore, indicating accelerating demand. ... ## Expansion and Capacity Utilization To address capacity constraints, Macpower has leased 13 acres (9+4 acres) near its existing plant in Rajkot for a 30-year term. The ₹50 crore investment will fund a state-of-the-art, centrally air-conditioned assembly facility spanning 1.5–2 lakh square feet, with targeted completion within 12 months. The project benefits from the Vikshit Gujarat New Industrial Policy 2026, offering a 25% capital subsidy and a 7% interest subsidy on debt, reducing effective borrowing costs to approximately 1.25%. Current capacity utilization is expected to reach over 90% for FY27, based on an existing capacity of 2,500 units. The new facility aims to de-bottleneck operations and enable backward integration. Management stated that average machine realization has risen to ₹20.9–21 lakh, with price increases of 4–6% implemented from June 1, 2026, to offset raw material cost pressures.

headline: North America Electronics Manufacturing Services Market
summary_text: The North America electronics manufacturing services market was valued at USD 197.22 billion in 2025 and is projected to increase from USD 207.98 billion in 2026 to USD 283.91 billion by 2031. The market is expected to record a CAGR of 6.42% during the 2026-2031 forecast period, supported by semiconductor reshoring, automotive electronics demand, AI-server production and increased outsourcing of complex manufacturing operations. ... CHIPS and Science Act Incentives Accelerate Regional Manufacturing Government incentives are strengthening the North American electronics supply chain and encouraging investment in domestic production. Awards totaling USD 36.4 billion across 40 fabrication and packaging projects by late 2025 generated additional demand for nearby electronics assembly capacity. Contract manufacturers are colocating surface-mount production lines near semiconductor fabrication facilities, enabling integrated wafer-to-board supply chains that reduce lead times and logistics exposure. Jabil's USD 500 million North Carolina project, announced in mid-2025, reflects the growing alignment between advanced packaging, box-build capacity, AI infrastructure and high-performance computing demand. Reshoring Initiative data also showed that 287,299 U.S. manufacturing jobs were announced in 2023, with electrical equipment and electronics leading repatriation activity. Section 48D tax credits are expected to support continued capital investment through 2028, helping sustain above-trend growth in the North America electronics manufacturing services market. ... Key Market Growth Factors - Rising demand for rapid NPI turn-around in regulated medical devices - Expansion of AI-server and high-speed computing hardware production - Increased outsourcing of system integration, testing and regulatory documentation - Greater demand for resilient North American electronics supply chains - Ongoing margin pressure from Asian high-volume contract manufacturers Box-Build and Hybrid Manufacturing Models Gain Momentum Electromechanical assembly and box build represent the fastest-growing service category, with revenue projected to rise at a 6.72% CAGR. Defense contractors and medical-device manufacturers increasingly outsource final integration, system-level testing, regulatory documentation and thermal-solution co-design. Printed-circuit-board assembly accounted for 42.76% of market value in 2025, although demand is shifting from commodity placement toward high-reliability Class 3 production. AI-server growth is also increasing demand for enclosure, cold-plate and cable-assembly expertise. The North America electronics manufacturing services market for box-build work is forecast to approach USD 40 billion by 2031, representing approximately one-quarter of regional market value as turnkey programs replace board-level contracts. Contract manufacturing held a 64.58% market share in 2025, supported by established relationships in industrial automation, telecommunications and automotive electronics. However, hybrid and turnkey models are projected to grow at a 6.81% CAGR as customers seek consolidated responsibility for procurement, design verification, compliance and production. These agreements are gaining traction in AI infrastructure, medical devices, automotive electronics and defense applications, where supply resilience and manufacturing flexibility increasingly outweigh marginal cost considerations.

headline: Silgan and AIP to Acquire Trivium Packaging in $3.4 Billion Metal Packaging Deal
summary_text: Silgan Holdings Inc. agreed on Oct. 19, 2026, to combine its metal food can and flat cap closures operations with Netherlands-based Trivium Packaging B.V. in a new company backed by funds affiliated with American Industrial Partners. The Norwalk, Connecticut, packaging maker said the new venture, Silgan Metal Containers and Closures, will buy Trivium in an all-cash deal that values the European metal packaging supplier at about $3.4 billion in enterprise value, including debt. Silgan will own 60% of the new company and consolidate it, while AIP funds will hold the remaining 40%. ... ## Key developments - Silgan MCC will combine Silgan's Metal Containers segment and its Food and Beverage Flat Cap Closures businesses, valued at about $3.8 billion, with Trivium, valued at about $3.4 billion. - Silgan will receive about $2.3 billion in cash, which it plans to use to retire certain existing debt, and AIP funds will contribute about $1.0 billion of cash equity. - Silgan's remaining Dispensing and Custom Containers businesses will be grouped into a new wholly owned segment, Silgan Dispensing Solutions. - Trivium's owners, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and Ardagh Group, are selling their stakes; Ardagh said it expects about $90 million in net cash for its roughly 42% holding. - Silgan's board approved the deal unanimously, and closing is expected in mid-2027 after regulatory approvals and works council consultations. ... ## Competitive and supply chain implications Metal packaging relies on a concentrated base of tinplate and aluminum sheet suppliers, and steel and aluminum costs have been exposed to trade measures on both sides of the Atlantic. A larger buyer with plants in North America and Europe gains more flexibility to shift volumes between mills and regions. Silgan said the combination will improve supply security for customers, in addition to widening geographic reach and product range. The deal also changes the landscape for rival can makers such as Crown Holdings, Ball Corp. and Ardagh Metal Packaging, as well as regional European producers. Trivium brings specialty and branded metal packaging that complements Silgan's food can base, while Silgan's flat cap closures add metal lids for jars and bottles. Customers that tender across several suppliers may see fewer independent bidders for some European contracts, which makes the competition reviews a closing condition to watch.

summary_text: # Fathom Digital Manufacturing Expands Aerospace and Defense Platform with Three Strategic Acquisitions Acquisitions of TCS Industries, TCS Electronics and Precision Grinding & Manufacturing strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities as the industry seeks greater production capacity and more resilient supply chains CHICAGO, IL & AUSTIN, TX – October 13, 2026 – CORE Industrial Partners (“CORE”), a manufacturing, industrial technology and industrial services-focused private equity firm, today announced that its portfolio company, Fathom Digital Manufacturing (“Fathom”), has acquired TCS Industries, TCS Electronics (collectively, “TCS”) and Precision Grinding & Manufacturing Corporation (“PGM”), expanding its precision manufacturing capabilities and presence in the aerospace and defense markets. The acquisitions advance Fathom’s strategy to build a leading U.S. precision manufacturing platform at a time when aerospace and defense companies are seeking to strengthen domestic supply chains, augment production capacity and bring increasingly complex technologies to market. By combining advanced manufacturing, electronics integration and specialized production capabilities, Fathom is better positioned to support customers from early-stage development and prototyping through qualified, sustained production. TCS and PGM bring decades of aerospace and defense experience, longstanding customer relationships and complementary capabilities spanning precision machining, electronics manufacturing, complex assemblies and specialized finishing. The acquisitions increase Fathom’s nationwide footprint to 10 facilities and approximately 700 employees, creating additional capacity to support technically demanding programs while helping customers address production bottlenecks and reduce supply chain complexity. ... Headquartered in Hartland, Wisconsin, Fathom provides more than 25 advanced manufacturing services, including additive manufacturing, CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, injection molding, tooling, assembly, finishing and engineering support. The addition of TCS and PGM further reinforces Fathom’s ability to address growing demand for precision components, integrated electronics and complex assemblies, particularly as customers look to streamline supplier relationships and move more efficiently from development into production. ... TCS Industries and TCS Electronics, based in Rochester, New York, have nearly 35 years of experience supporting aerospace and defense customers. Their capabilities include precision CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, aluminum dip brazing, welding, electro-mechanical box builds, PCB assemblies and cable and wire harnesses. TCS operates two facilities totaling more than 200,000 square feet and has built a reputation for quality, responsiveness and technical execution. > “For nearly 35 years, we’ve built TCS around the trust of our customers and the expertise of our employees,” said Manoj Shekar, founder and President of TCS. “Joining Fathom gives us the resources and broader capabilities to build on that success while maintaining the customer focus and operating discipline that have defined our business. We’re excited about the opportunities ahead for our employees and customers.” ... Precision Grinding & Manufacturing, also headquartered in Rochester, brings nearly six decades of experience in precision manufacturing, including CNC machining, milling, turning, grinding, lapping, honing, assembly and specialized finishing. PGM supports aerospace and defense customers from low- and mid-volume manufacturing through full-rate production, with expertise in technically demanding components requiring rigorous quality control and documentation. ... Both TCS and PGM hold AS9100 certifications and ITAR registrations, further strengthening Fathom’s capabilities in highly regulated markets.

summary_text: GreenSeed and R.A. Jones GreenSeed External Manufacturing turned to R.A. Jones and the Alterion CL-170 to enhance its cartoning operations. October 8, 2026 GreenSeed External Manufacturing, a contract packager based in Batavia, Illinois, has served brand owners and retailers for more than half a century. When the company, which packages dry foods, dry pet food, nutraceuticals and supplements, had the opportunity to take on a major job from one of its largest customers, GreenSeed needed to upgrade its cartoning capabilities – and quickly. GreenSeed turned to R.A. Jones and the Alterion CL-170 to meet demand with a flexible and efficient solution. ... FE: How would you describe GreenSeed’s packaging capabilities? SR: GreenSeed packaging capabilities include horizontal form, fill and seal pouches, with and without a zipper or gusset, in a wide variety of sizes; vertical form, fill, and seal pouches in a wide variety of sizes; stick packs in 23 mm, 35 mm, and 45 mm sizes; fiber board, metal seamed canisters and PET canisters; and secondary packaging for retail, club store and DTC. ... FE: What drew GreenSeed to the Alterion? SR: We knew we needed a dedicated cartoner that combined operator-assisted loading with automated cartoning to bridge a critical gap and meet the rigorous demands of a bag-in-box project of this size. But what we didn’t have on our side was time. Most OEMs were quoting us 8- to 12-month lead times, which was an automatic non-starter for our necessary production schedule. We turned to a longtime trusted partner, R.A Jones, a global leader in cartoning and packaging technology and a solid reputation in the industry. They had just built a new machine – the Alterion CL-170 – to unveil at PACK EXPO Las Vegas (fall 2025), designed specifically for contract packagers and regional brand owners looking for high-end reliability in a mid-speed footprint. R.A Jones made the deal happen fast. The Alterion gave us the technical sophistication, superior OEE and quick changeover flexibility we needed to run two lines into a single cartoner and hit our customer’s deadline on schedule. ... FE: What benefits has GreenSeed experienced since integrating the Alterion? SR: The Alterion has performed seamlessly from Day 1. We were literally running bags into boxes the same day R.A Jones installed the new cartoner at our plant. Since going into production in late December, the Alterion has had virtually zero operational downtime, enabling us to increase overall OEE by 5% to 7%. The servo-driven barrel loader and adjustable U-shaped buckets allow us to load pouches consistently into two multiple carton sizes without fail and carton scrap has dropped below 1%. Automating the cartoning step enabled us to reassign operators to higher-value roles on the floor, including lines that are more labor intensive. Right now, we run the machine at an optimized gross speed of 120 cpm to meet the customer’s monthly volume, which delivers a 97%+ attainment rate. However, knowing that we have the capability to dial it up to 170 cpm gives us the option of adding a third VFFS line into the feed down the road. Having this flexibility is not only comforting for our team but the customer's planning team as well.

headline: Supremex blames tariffs as it plans to cut 6% of workforce | Packaging Dive
summary_text: ### Dive Brief: - Montreal-based paper packaging and envelopes maker Supremex announced a restructuring plan Tuesday as it estimated a $10 million to $12 million hit to annualized operating earnings from tariffs. - The plan has three primary focuses. Supremex will consolidate certain U.S. and Canadian envelope locations into more efficient “centres of excellence;” shrink its Saint-Laurent, Quebec, commercial print facility and transfer folding carton production to its flagship folding carton facility in Lachine, Quebec; and accelerate technology deployment for “core back-office processes.” - The company is eliminating 6% of its workforce, or 60 positions. Supremex projects the plan will lead to $5.7 million in annualized cost savings across Q4 2026 and Q1 2027. Still, the company says this has no impact on growth strategy and investments. ... Wood products, pulp and paper were caught up on both sides of American and Canadian tariffs announced in August and September. Supremex works across the neighboring countries, operating nine manufacturing facilities across four Canadian provinces as well as four manufacturing facilities across three U.S. states. Supremex leadership “believes the current tariff environment will prove temporary” but is operating under the assumption they will remain. ... This comes after Supremex recently announced a $4 million investment to enhance folding carton and e-commerce packaging operations in the Indianapolis and Chicago areas. It also acquired Toronto-area carton specialist Goldrich Printpak, which reportedly had annual sales of about $30 million. Supremex says it’s still moving forward with its growth strategy. “Supremex continues to pursue targeted acquisitions in packaging, advance the integration of its recently acquired businesses, and invest in the capabilities that support its long-term transformation into a diversified North American leader in paper-based packaging,” according to the announcement.

headline: AZCO Corp. Launches Vertical Pouch Making Machine | Packaging Strategies
summary_text: AZCO Corporation has launched the Securus VS610 Vertical Pouch Making Machine, a USA-made packaging solution designed to support medical device manufacturers and healthcare suppliers seeking greater control over pouch production, faster changeovers, and seamless integration into automated packaging lines. As manufacturers across medical, industrial, electronics, and specialty product markets face increasing pressure to reduce lead times, manage packaging costs, and respond quickly to changing product requirements, the VS610 offers a practical alternative to relying on premade pouches. The machine allows users to produce secure, sealed pouches on demand using rollstock materials such as Tyvek®, poly films, and foils, eliminating the need to stock multiple pouch sizes and materials. ... The VS610 was engineered to support a wide range of packaging applications where flexibility, repeatability, and reliable sealing performance are critical. Its compact vertical design simplifies operation while maintaining consistent pouch quality across materials and formats. The system supports pouch sizes ranging from 2” x 2” up to 6” x 10”, making it suitable for a variety of products, kits, and components. Proven sealing technology helps ensure package integrity, while optional inspection and validation features are available for applications that require additional process control. ... ### Quick-Change Tooling for High-Mix, Low-Volume Production Many medical device manufacturers operate in high-mix, low- to medium-volume production environments where frequent changeovers are unavoidable. The VS610 addresses this challenge with quick-change, tool-less adjustments that allow operators to switch pouch sizes in under a minute. Setup is straightforward: slot in the right tool, enter the bag length, and begin production. This rapid changeover capability minimizes downtime and makes it practical to run multiple products or SKUs on a single machine without sacrificing efficiency. ... ### Built for Automation and Line Integration In addition to standalone operation, the VS610 is designed to integrate easily into automated packaging lines. The system can be paired with robotic loading, scale feeders, conveyors, and downstream equipment, allowing manufacturers to build scalable, semi-automated, or fully automated solutions. Optional configurations include horizontal feed arrangements, infeed and takeaway conveyors, and reject handling systems. These capabilities make the VS610 well suited for manufacturers looking to incrementally automate packaging operations without investing in large, inflexible machinery.

headline: PMMI’s 2026 State of the Industry Report Reveals a Packaging Machinery Market Driven by Flexibility, Automation, and New North American Opportunities
summary_text: September 14, 2026 Herndon, Va; Sep. 14, 2026 – PMMI, The Association for Packaging and Processing Technologies, announced the release of its 2026 Packaging State of the Industry Report and accompanying infographic, which finds the U.S. packaging machinery market reached an estimated $11.7 billion in shipment value in 2025, with food accounting for approximately 44% of the total. The report also finds Canadian domestic packaging machinery shipments reached approximately $1.2 billion in 2025, up 3.6% from 2024, underscoring continued opportunities across the North American packaging machinery market. Key Findings from the 2026 Packaging State of the Industry Report - U.S. packaging machinery shipment value reached an estimated $11.7 billion in 2025. - Food remained the largest U.S. end market at approximately 44% of the total, with food machinery shipments estimated at $5.1 billion in 2025 and projected to reach approximately $7.1 billion by 2031. - Canadian domestic packaging machinery shipments reached approximately $1.2 billion in 2025, up 3.6% from 2024, and are expected to approach $1.4 billion in 2027. - The U.S. was Canada’s largest source of packaging machinery imports in 2025, accounting for 30%, while 91% of Canadian packaging machinery exports were destined for the United States. - SKU proliferation, emerging AI applications, workforce constraints, sustainability and regulatory requirements, and rising input costs are among the forces influencing equipment decisions. ... The report finds the U.S. packaging machinery market reached an estimated $11.7 billion in shipment value in 2025, with food remaining the largest end market at approximately 44% of the total. Food machinery shipments alone totaled an estimated $5.1 billion and are projected to reach approximately $7.1 billion by 2031. Beverage, pharmaceutical, and other key end markets are also expected to continue generating opportunities for packaging machinery suppliers. At the same time, the industry is being transformed by changing consumer behavior and manufacturing priorities. Interviews conducted for the study point to SKU proliferation, emerging AI applications, workforce constraints, tighter capital discipline, sustainability and regulatory requirements, and rising input costs as some of the most important forces influencing equipment decisions. Social-media-driven demand and changing consumer preferences are accelerating the need for machinery capable of frequent changeovers and handling a greater variety of package formats, including single-serve and grab-and-go options. ... The report provides a complete view of equipment demand and market dynamics across North America. Canadian domestic packaging machinery shipments reached approximately $1.2 billion in 2025, up 3.6% from 2024, and are expected to approach $1.3 billion in 2026 and $1.4 billion in 2027. Food represents the largest Canadian end market, accounting for 43.6% of 2025 machinery value. The data underscores the deeply connected nature of the North American market. Canada imported approximately $504 million in packaging machinery in 2025, with the U.S. representing its largest source at 30% of imports. Canada exported approximately $550 million in machinery, with 91% of those exports destined for the United States. ... What Is Driving Packaging Machinery Investment? One of the clearest themes in the report is manufacturers’ growing need for flexible, adaptable automation. More SKUs, shorter runs, changing package formats, and greater product variety are pushing manufacturers away from dedicated equipment toward systems designed for faster changeovers and greater operational flexibility. At the end of the line, case erecting, packing, and sealing are increasingly converging into integrated systems, while robotic palletizing is gaining traction in applications with frequently changing SKUs, case sizes, and pallet configurations. Persistent labor challenges are adding urgency to automation investments. Palletizing, for example, remains a prime target because of the repetitive and physically demanding nature of the work. Robotic systems and cobots are providing manufacturers with a broader range of options to improve throughput, ergonomics, and workforce utilization, although cost, speed, and integration requirements continue to determine which technologies are best suited to individual applications. ... How Are Sustainability and Regulation Affecting Packaging Machinery? Sustainability and regulation are creating another layer of complexity. Extended Producer Responsibility policies and restrictions on single-use plastics are influencing material choices and packaging design, increasing demand for machinery capable of accommodating a broader range of substrates and formats. Manufacturers are also showing greater interest in modular and upgradeable systems that allow operations to adapt as regulations and material requirements evolve.
